features.feature: Multi-track timeline (V/A/T tracks, add/remove, mute, lock, per-track height)
features.note: ui.tsx NEW_DOC builds V1/V2/T1/A1/A2; Timeline component + onAddTrack/onRemoveTrack/onTrackToggle (ui.tsx ~1199-1221, 1346-1556). Solid foundation.

features.feature: Trim / split (razor) / ripple delete / duplicate clips
features.note: ui.tsx splitAt (549), rippleDelete (594), duplicateClip (582), onTrimClip with frame-accurate srcStart/srcEnd math (1173-1187). Razor tool 'c' shortcut.

features.feature: Drag-to-move clips with snapping (clip edges + playhead)
features.note: Timeline snappedT() snaps to 0/playhead/clip starts+ends within 0.25s (ui.tsx 1376-1389). Snap toggle in toolbar.

features.feature: Frame-accurate WYSIWYG preview (canvas compositor, scrubbing, J/K/L, frame step)
features.note: drawPreviewFrame composites every video track + PiP transform + text per frame (ui.tsx 607-689) via WebCodecsPlayer.frameAt; J/K/L + arrow frame-step shortcuts (994-998). Genuinely strong.

features.feature: Picture-in-picture / overlay / transform (scale, position, rotation)
features.note: VideoClip.transform {x,y,scale,rotation}; preview drawVideoFrame + export drawClipFrame apply identical center-anchored transform (ui.tsx 1289-1344; compositor.ts 174-181). Transform (PiP) inspector panel (1604-1620).

features.feature: Speed change (per-clip, video + audio)
features.note: clip.speed wired into clipDuration, srcTime sampling, and audio playbackRate in mixAudio (compositor.ts 313). UI slider 50-200% (ui.tsx 1569).

features.feature: Text titles with font/size/color/weight/outline + position + entrance animation
features.note: TextClip + TextDialog (ui.tsx 1728-1752); drawTextClip renders fade/slide-up/pop with outline, multi-line, baseline scaling, in both preview and export (compositor.ts 205-239). No mid-clip text keyframing though.

features.feature: Per-clip volume + audio fade in/out + master volume
features.note: AudioClip fadeIn/fadeOut + master volume mixed via OfflineAudioContext gain ramps (compositor.ts 304-334); master fade applyMasterFade (337).

features.feature: Aspect-ratio presets (16:9, 9:16, 1:1, 4:5, 4K) for project + export
features.note: PRESETS array incl vertical/square/insta/4K (ui.tsx 161-168); NewDialog + ExportDialog. capQuality preserves project aspect on export (compositor.ts 381-403).

features.feature: Export to MP4 (H.264) on-device, hardware-accelerated with fallback
features.note: exportTimeline → WebCodecs VideoEncoder + mp4-muxer CDN, ffmpeg.wasm image2 frame-pipe fallback, AAC audio mux (compositor.ts 407-571). Device-tier resolution/fps caps for free tier.

features.feature: Undo/redo history + project save/open (local library)
features.note: UndoStack(60) commit/undo/redo (ui.tsx 254-265); saveProject/loadProject to local library — but media files must be re-imported on open (loadFromLibrary 927-940, toast 'Files need to be reimported'). Weaker than rivals' cloud projects.

features.feature: Crossfade / transition between clips (fade, slide, wipe, dissolve)
features.note: editor.ts concatClips has full xfade chain (fade/slide/wipe, 104-122) AND VideoClip carries transition/transDur fields — but the live WYSIWYG compositor (compositor.ts) does NOT render any cross-clip transition; only per-clip text anim + opacity keyframes. So transitions exist in dead concat path, not in what actually exports. Needs porting into renderTimelineFrame (blend overlapping clips).

features.feature: Stickers / shapes / emoji / image overlays from a library
features.note: Images can be imported and placed as video clips with PiP transform (addClipFromMedia, kind image). But there is no built-in sticker/shape/emoji/GIF library or vector shape tool. Feasible browser-only: ship an SVG/emoji sticker set + a rect/ellipse/arrow shape primitive drawn on canvas; reuse the transform path. No model needed.

features.feature: Keyframe animation of clip properties (position/scale/opacity/color over time)
features.note: AnimatedParam keyframes exist for brightness/contrast/saturation/hue/opacity with ease-in-out, sampled in preview+export (ui.tsx AnimatableSlider 1767-1818; compositor sampleParam 94-98). MISSING: keyframing the PiP transform (x/y/scale/rotation) — that's the motion-graphics workhorse (Ken Burns, fly-ins). transform is static-only. Make transform an AnimatedParam set — small, same machinery.

features.feature: Professional color grading: color wheels (lift/gamma/gain) + RGB curves + scopes
features.note: ColorWheelsPanel + RgbCurvesPanel per clip, applied to pixels in preview + export (ui.tsx 1621-1634; compositor.ts 188-201); histogram/waveform/vectorscope scopes (showScopes, renderHistogram/renderWaveformScope/renderVectorscope, ui.tsx 696-715, 1047-1061). 14 preset LUT-style grades. This genuinely rivals DaVinci's basics.

features.feature: Auto-reframe / Magic Resize (smart-crop one project to 9:16/1:1/16:9 keeping subject)
features.note: No reframe. Matters hugely for social repurposing (one of the top reasons creators use CapCut/Canva/Premiere). Feasible on-device: run MediaPipe selfie/object segmentation (~3MB) or a saliency pass per keyframe to pick crop center, then animate the existing transform/fit. with-cdn-lib + small model.

features.feature: Chroma key / green-screen removal
features.rival: DaVinci, Premiere, Final Cut, CapCut, Veed, Kapwing
features.note: No chroma key. Table-stakes for any 'pro' claim and common in web tools. Fully feasible browser-only with zero model: per-pixel key in a WebGL shader or in the existing getImageData grade pass (key color + similarity + smoothness + spill suppression). Add as a clip effect alongside curves. Effort modest, high credibility payoff.

features.feature: AI background removal (person matting, no green screen)
features.note: No subject matting. The image studio reportedly has remove-background; video needs per-frame matting. Feasible on-device: MediaPipe Selfie Segmentation (~3MB) or RobustVideoMatting/MODNet ONNX (~25-100MB, well under 180MB) via onnxruntime-web; composite the alpha each frame in renderTimelineFrame. needs-model but small.

features.feature: Auto-captions / subtitles (speech-to-text, timed, styled, burn-in)
features.rival: all rivals (CapCut, Veed, Kapwing, Clipchamp, Canva, Premiere, DaVinci 20)
features.note: THE biggest single gap-vs-reality finding: on-device Whisper transcription ALREADY EXISTS in the suite (engines/subtitle/auto.ts videoToCaptions → timed chunks → SRT/VTT/burn-in, whisper tiny/base ~75-150MB) and is used by a separate auto-subtitle tool + dub.ts. It is simply NOT wired into the Video Studio timeline (ui.tsx imports only getVideoInfo + compositor). Wiring videoToCaptions → auto-create TextClips on the T track = transformative and reuses shipped, in-budget on-device code. Highest-leverage item.

features.feature: Text-to-speech AI voiceover from a script
features.note: On-device TTS already exists (engines/tts/studio.ts speakToBuffer + VOICE_STYLES, used by dub.ts) and on-device translate. Not exposed in Video Studio. Add a 'Generate voiceover' action that synthesizes to an AudioBuffer → drops an AudioClip on A2. Reuses shipped engines; feasible and on-device.

features.feature: Text-based editing (edit video by editing the transcript; delete words/filler removes footage)
features.note: No transcript-driven editing. This is Premiere's headline workflow + a Kapwing/Veed staple. Feasible on-device by composing what we already have: videoToCaptions gives word/segment timings → render an editable transcript → deleting a span maps to splitAt + ripple-delete on the clip. No new model (reuses Whisper). High effort (timing→edit mapping + UI) but uniquely differentiating and 100% on-device.

features.feature: Remove silences / filler words / auto jump-cut (Smart Cut)
features.note: No silence detection. Feasible fully on-device with NO model: analyze the decoded AudioBuffer RMS (we already decode all audio in mixAudio) to find sub-threshold gaps > N ms, then auto split+ripple them out. Reuses Web Audio + existing split/ripple. Cheap, high creator value.

features.feature: Auto-detect scene cuts / scene split on import
features.rival: DaVinci (Scene Cut Detect), Premiere, Final Cut
features.note: No automatic scene detection. Feasible on-device with no model: sample frames via the existing WebCodecsPlayer.frameAt, compute frame-difference/histogram delta, split at spikes. Reuses the decode path + splitAt. Medium effort, nice-to-have for 'pro'.

features.feature: Stabilization
features.note: No stabilization. Hardest item to do well on-device (optical-flow / feature-track + smoothing). Possible via ffmpeg.wasm vidstabdetect/vidstabtransform if the build includes libvidstab (ours likely doesn't) or a custom WASM. Lower priority — heavy and not a primary differentiator for the target users.

features.feature: Motion tracking (attach text/mask/effect to a moving object)
features.note: No tracker. Feasible-ish on-device: a lightweight KLT/optical-flow point tracker in WASM or a small ONNX tracker drives keyframes on the transform of a text/PiP clip. Pairs with transform-keyframing. Hard, do after transform keyframes land.

features.feature: Audio: noise reduction / speech enhancement / ducking
features.rival: DaVinci (Voice Isolation/Ducker), Premiere (Enhance Speech), Veed, Kapwing
features.note: Master chain exists for the Audio Studio (BS.1770 loudness per the suite notes) but Video Studio's mixAudio applies only gain + fades — no NR/EQ/compression/ducking. Feasible on-device: ducking is trivial (sidechain music gain to the voice track's RMS, all in OfflineAudioContext). Noise suppression via RNNoise WASM (~85KB) or a small DTLN ONNX. Reuse the Audio Studio master chain here.

features.feature: Stock media + royalty-free music/SFX library, brand kit
features.note: No stock library, no brand kit. Templates exist (28 in 7 categories, VIDEO_TEMPLATES) but they ship no media — user must supply everything (applyTemplate toast 'drop your media in', ui.tsx 488). Partly a content/licensing problem, not purely technical; a curated CDN-hosted CC0 clip/music set + a saved brand palette/font/logo is feasible browser-only. Lower eng priority.

features.feature: Screen + webcam recorder built in
features.note: No capture. Feasible browser-only with getDisplayMedia + getUserMedia + MediaRecorder → import the recording straight into the media pool. No model, modest effort, rounds out the 'create' story.

features.feature: Real-time multi-user collaboration / cloud projects / review comments
features.note: Local-only projects (IndexedDB-style library) and re-import-on-open. Real-time collab conflicts with the no-server, on-device constraint; the suite's P2P stack (Send/WebRTC) could enable peer share but true Google-Docs-style co-edit is out of scope. Mark not a near-term target.

features.feature: Generative video / generative extend / AI b-roll
features.note: Not feasible under the constraints. Generative video needs server GPUs and multi-GB models — violates no-server + <=180MB on-device. Correctly out of scope; do not chase.

features.feature: Crop / pan within frame (non-uniform crop tool)
features.note: fit contain/cover + PiP transform (scale/position) cover most reframing, and preview pinch/pan exists (usePinchPan). But there is no explicit rectangular CROP tool that changes the source region (we only scale/letterbox). A true crop = set source rect into drawImage; small addition to drawClipFrame.

features.feature: Adjustment layer / apply grade or effect across clips at once
features.note: applyGradeToAll applies a preset grade to every clip in one shot (ui.tsx 504-518), but there is no persistent adjustment layer/track that affects clips beneath it; per-clip only. An adjustment-track concept would let one curve/wheel set ride over a range. Medium effort.

topGaps.title: Wire on-device auto-captions into the timeline (Whisper → auto TextClips)
topGaps.approach: The transcription engine is ALREADY in the repo and in-budget: engines/subtitle/auto.ts videoToCaptions(file,{size:'tiny'|'base'}) returns timed chunks using Whisper (tiny ~75MB / base ~150MB, both <=180MB) via onnxruntime-web/transformers.js, already used by the auto-subtitle tool and dub.ts. Add a 'Auto-captions' action in Video Studio: run videoToCaptions on the selected video clip's media File, then create one TextClip per chunk on the T track at chunk.start/end with a caption preset (bottom, outline). Reuse existing TextClip render path (already burns into preview + export). Add a caption style picker. Every single rival has this; we have the parts and just haven't connected them — the highest-leverage move.

topGaps.title: Auto-reframe / smart resize one project to 9:16 / 1:1 / 16:9
topGaps.approach: This is the #1 reason creators reach for CapCut/Canva/Premiere. Add MediaPipe Selfie Segmentation (~3MB) or a saliency/object detector via CDN; sample frames with the existing WebCodecsPlayer.frameAt at ~2fps, compute the subject's center per sample, then keyframe the existing PiP transform (after transform-keyframing lands) so the crop tracks the subject as the project re-aspects. Falls back to center-crop when no subject. Output stays WYSIWYG because it just drives transform+fit we already render.

topGaps.title: Make the PiP transform keyframable (motion graphics / Ken Burns / fly-ins)
topGaps.approach: Transform (x/y/scale/rotation) is currently static (VideoClip.transform). Color params already use AnimatedParam keyframes end-to-end. Convert transform into the same AnimatedParam machinery (makeStatic/addKeyframe/sampleAnimated) and sample it in drawVideoFrame (ui.tsx) + drawClipFrame (compositor.ts). Pure reuse of shipped keyframe code; unlocks pans/zooms/slides AND is the prerequisite for auto-reframe and motion tracking. Browser-only, no model.

topGaps.title: Render real cross-clip transitions in the WYSIWYG compositor
topGaps.approach: Transitions are a phantom feature: editor.ts concatClips fully implements fade/slide/wipe xfade and VideoClip carries transition/transDur, but the live compositor (compositor.ts renderTimelineFrame) ignores them, so what users preview/export has none. In renderTimelineFrame, when two clips on the same track overlap within transDur (or use an explicit transition region), draw the outgoing clip then the incoming with a time-based globalAlpha (fade) or a clip-rect/translate (wipe/slide). Mirror in drawPreviewFrame for WYSIWYG. No new deps.

topGaps.title: Remove-silences / Smart-Cut (RMS gap detection → auto ripple)
topGaps.approach: Zero new models. We already decode every clip's audio to AudioBuffer in mixAudio (compositor.ts). Reuse that: compute windowed RMS over a clip's audio, find runs below a user threshold longer than N ms (with lead/tail padding), and emit a list of split+ripple-delete ops using the existing splitAt + rippleDelete. Add a one-click 'Remove silences' with sensitivity + min-gap controls. Big creator time-saver; matches CapCut/Kapwing/DaVinci IntelliCut, fully on-device.

topGaps.title: Chroma key (green-screen) clip effect
topGaps.approach: No model needed. Add a per-clip chromaKey {color,similarity,smoothness,spill} effect. Easiest path: WebGL shader pass per frame (key color distance → alpha, spill suppression); cheaper path: extend the existing getImageData grade block in drawClipFrame/drawVideoFrame to zero alpha for matching pixels. Composites naturally over lower video tracks the compositor already stacks. Table-stakes for the 'pro' claim and present in nearly every rival including the web ones.

topGaps.title: On-device AI background removal (person matting, no green screen)
topGaps.approach: Every web rival (CapCut/Veed/Kapwing/Canva/Clipchamp) has one-click background removal. Use MediaPipe Selfie Segmentation (~3MB, real-time) for the fast path, or RobustVideoMatting/MODNet ONNX (~25-100MB, under 180MB) via onnxruntime-web for quality; produce a per-frame alpha and composite in renderTimelineFrame over the lower tracks. Cache masks per source frame to keep export tractable. Pairs with chroma key under one 'Remove background' clip effect.

topGaps.title: AI voiceover from script + auto-dub, surfaced in the Studio
topGaps.approach: Reuse shipped engines: engines/tts/studio.ts speakToBuffer + VOICE_STYLES and engines/video/dub.ts already do text→speech and full transcribe→translate→dub on-device. Add two Studio actions: (1) 'Voiceover from script' → speakToBuffer → AudioClip on A2; (2) 'Auto-dub' → dubVideo → replacement AudioClip. Models are the small TTS + Whisper-tiny already in budget. Closes the TTS gap CapCut/Veed/Clipchamp lead on.

topGaps.title: Transcript / text-based editing
topGaps.approach: Premiere's flagship workflow, also in Kapwing/Veed/DaVinci 20. Build on the same videoToCaptions output (word/segment timings, Whisper, in-budget): render an editable transcript panel; selecting/deleting a span maps timings → splitAt + rippleDelete on the underlying clip; reordering maps to clip moves. No new model, but substantial timing↔edit-mapping + UI work. Schedule after captions wiring (shares the transcription plumbing) — uniquely differentiating and fully on-device.

topGaps.title: Sticker / shape / emoji library + built-in screen & webcam recorder
topGaps.approach: Two cheap rounding-out features. Stickers/shapes: ship an SVG/emoji set + rect/ellipse/arrow primitives drawn on canvas, placed via the existing PiP transform path (no model). Recorder: getDisplayMedia + getUserMedia + MediaRecorder → drop the recording into the media pool. Both browser-only, no model; together they match the 'capture + decorate' expectations set by CapCut/Canva/Clipchamp/Veed.

features.feature: Raster layers with reorder / duplicate / delete / lock / visibility / opacity
features.rival: Photoshop, Affinity, GIMP, Photopea, Pixlr, Picsart
features.note: ui.tsx: Layer union (image/paint/text/shape/adjust), addLayer/removeLayer/duplicateLayer/moveLayer, LayerRow toggle/lock. Solid.

features.feature: Full blend-mode set (multiply/screen/overlay/dodge/burn/hue/sat/color/lum etc.)
features.note: ui.tsx BLEND_LIST = all 16 canvas globalCompositeOperation blend modes, applied in compositeDoc per layer.

features.feature: Non-destructive layer masks (paint to hide/reveal, mask from selection, feathered)
features.note: ui.tsx addMaskToLayer + strokeAt mask-edit mode (brush reveals white / eraser hides black, soft brush feathers), destination-in composite. Genuinely non-destructive.

features.feature: Adjustment layers honoring opacity + blend + mask (bright/contrast, hue-sat, levels, curves, color-balance, invert)
features.note: ui.tsx applyAdjustmentBelow + compositeDoc: adjusted-below mixed back over original at opacity, blend, and mask (comment documents the prior bug fix). Real adjustment-layer semantics.

features.feature: Per-channel Curves (master + R/G/B, arbitrary draggable points, smooth interp)
features.note: color-wheels.ts applyCurveSet/buildLut (smoothstep), CurveSet master+r+g+b; ui.tsx curves adjust layer seeds identity CurveSet, RgbCurvesPanel editor. Matches Photoshop Curves.

features.feature: Levels (black/white input, gamma, output range)
features.note: ui.tsx applyAdjustmentBelow 'levels' builds LUT from blackIn/whiteIn/gamma/blackOut/whiteOut.

features.feature: Layer styles: drop shadow, outer glow, stroke, gradient overlay
features.note: layer-styles.ts applyLayerStyles covers shadow/glow/stroke/gradient. MISS vs rivals: inner shadow, inner glow, bevel/emboss, pattern overlay, color overlay, satin. Easy S-effort additions to same module.

features.feature: Selections: rectangle/ellipse marquee, freehand lasso, magic wand (color tolerance flood)
features.note: ui.tsx magicWand (BFS flood, tol^2*3), lassoMask, rectMask(+ellipse). Selection rendered as marching-difference overlay.

features.feature: Selection refine: feather, grow/contract, smooth, polygonal lasso, add/subtract/intersect modes
features.note: Selection is a single replace-only mask, no feather/grow/boolean combine. Matters because every real composite needs soft edges + additive selecting. Feasible browser-only: morphological dilate/erode + gaussianBlur on the mask alpha (gaussianBlur already in lib); add Shift/Alt combine in onPointerUp. No model needed.

features.feature: Brush engine: soft/hard edge, size, opacity, flow
features.note: ui.tsx strokeAt: radial-gradient soft brush with hardness, brushOpacity+brushFlow, spacing-interpolated dabs; eraser + selection-masked painting.

features.feature: Pressure/tilt dynamics, custom/textured brush tips, brush presets
features.note: No PointerEvent pressure/tiltX use, no stamp tips. Matters for painting/retouch credibility. Feasible browser-only: e.pressure is already on PointerEvent (size/opacity scale = S effort); image-stamp tips via offscreen canvas pattern = M. No model.

features.feature: Eraser, paint bucket (contiguous fill), eyedropper, fg/bg color swap
features.note: ui.tsx eraser (destination-out + mask-aware), bucketFill flood, eyedropper from composite, 'x' swaps fg/bg.

features.feature: Crop, flip H/V, rotate (layer + 90deg)
features.note: ui.tsx crop tool reframes all layers, flipActive, rotateActive.

features.feature: Free Transform: scale + rotate + skew + distort + perspective with on-canvas handles
features.note: ImageLayer has scaleX/scaleY/rotation fields and renderLayer applies them, and transformActive state exists, but there is NO interactive handle UI for scale/rotate/skew/perspective (move only). Perspective/distort needs a 3x3 homography warp drawImage-via-WebGL or per-triangle canvas warp. Skew/scale handles = M browser-only; perspective = L (WebGL texture or glfx.js).

features.feature: Convolution + stylize filters: gaussian blur, sharpen, emboss, edge, pixelate, posterize, noise
features.note: ui.tsx runFilter + KERNELS (convolve3x3), gaussianBlur, pixelate, posterize, noise.

features.feature: Rich filter gallery: motion/lens/radial blur, distort (twirl/ripple/spherize), liquify/warp, oil/watercolor, vignette, lens correction, chromatic-aberration
features.note: Only 3x3 kernels + gaussian. Liquify is a flagship rival feature (Affinity has a whole Liquify Persona). Feasible browser-only: glfx.js (WebGL) gives swirl/bulge/lens/triangle-blur/ink/perspective for ~free; liquify = forward-mesh warp on GPU (M-L). No model. High visual payoff.

features.feature: Healing brush / spot heal / clone stamp (texture-aware retouch)
features.note: No retouch tooling at all — this is the single biggest 'feels like a toy' gap for photo work. Clone stamp = sample-offset draw (S, browser-only). Spot heal = Poisson/seamless-clone blend of a sampled patch (M, browser-only, pure canvas math). Frequency-separation heal can come later.

features.feature: Content-aware fill / AI object removal / inpainting (remove a person, heal the gap)
features.rival: Photoshop, Canva (Magic Eraser), Pixlr, Picsart, Figma
features.note: This is the headline 2025-26 feature on EVERY web rival and the top reason users reach for them. Feasible on-device: MI-GAN 512 ONNX (~20-30MB, used by open-source inpaint-web) or LaMa via onnxruntime-web + WebGPU/WASM fallback — well under 180MB. User brushes the mask (we already have brush+mask plumbing), model inpaints. needs-model but proven browser-only.

features.feature: AI background removal (one-click subject cutout)
features.rival: Photoshop, Canva, Pixlr, Picsart, Figma, Photopea(plugin)
features.note: ui.tsx runRemoveBg -> removeBackgroundAuto (on-device segmentation model) with removeBackgroundByLuma fast fallback; sets background transparent. Already a marquee feature.

features.feature: AI Select Subject / smart select (auto-mask the main object as an editable selection)
features.note: We can REMOVE bg but cannot turn the segmentation into a SELECTION/MASK to keep editing. Feasible: reuse the same removeBackgroundAuto matte, threshold its alpha into a SelectionPath.mask — small wrapper over code we already have (S effort). High leverage, near-free.

features.feature: Auto-enhance / one-tap fix (white balance + auto levels)
features.note: ui.tsx runAutoEnhance -> autoEnhance (lib/studios).

features.feature: Color grading: LUT-style preset grades + shadow/mid/highlight color wheels
features.note: COLOR_GRADES presets applied via adjust (ui.tsx applyColorGrade). color-wheels.ts applyColorWheelsToImageData (shadows/mid/highlights lift, luma-weighted) EXISTS but is NOT wired as an image-studio adjustment kind — only the Video Studio uses it. Wiring it in as a 'Color Wheels' adjustment layer = S, code already written.

features.feature: Text: font/size/weight/italic, alignment, letter-spacing, line-height, outline, shadow, multi-line
features.note: ui.tsx TextLayer + renderLayer text path (drawSpacedText, outline stroke, shadow).

features.feature: Text on a path, warped text, vertical text, web-font picker beyond 8 system fonts
features.note: FONTS is 8 hardcoded system fonts; no text-on-path/warp. Matters for posters/social. Browser-only: CanvasRenderingContext2D path text via measureText + manual glyph placement along a Path2D (M); fonts via Google Fonts CSS @font-face load (S). No model.

features.feature: Vector shapes: rect/ellipse fill+stroke+corner radius
features.note: ui.tsx ShapeLayer rect/ellipse, roundedRect, fill/stroke/strokeWidth/radius.

features.feature: Pen tool / editable vector paths, boolean ops, polygon/line/custom shapes, convert to selection
features.note: Only 2 primitive shapes, no bezier pen, no path editing, no booleans. Figma/Affinity-class users expect this. Browser-only: Path2D + draggable bezier handles for editing; boolean ops via a CDN lib (paper.js or polygon-clipping). M-L effort. No model.

features.feature: Layer groups/folders, clipping masks
features.note: layers[] is a flat array, no group nodes, no clip-to-below. Matters for organizing real documents. Browser-only: add a 'group' layer kind that composites children to an offscreen canvas then blends as one; clipping = destination-in against the layer below. M effort. No model.

features.feature: PSD import + export (open/save native Photoshop files)
features.note: PSD interop is Photopea's #1 reason-to-exist and a pro must-have for interoperating. We only save a proprietary IndexedDB project + flat PNG/JPG/WebP. Feasible browser-only with ag-psd (CDN, ~pure JS, no model): read PSD -> our layer model, and write layers back to .psd. Our layer/mask/blend model maps cleanly. L effort, very high differentiation for a browser tool.

features.feature: Smart objects (non-destructive embedded/linked source you can re-edit)
features.note: No smart-object container; transforms/filters on image layers are baked except curves/levels adjustment layers. Browser-only: keep original source canvas + a transform/filter stack rendered on demand (we already cache composites). M effort. No model.

features.feature: RAW develop (demosaic + per-channel tone/WB/lens before pixel edit)
features.note: fileToCanvas only decodes browser-native formats; no RAW. Matters for photographers. Browser-only is HARD: libraw.wasm can decode RAW to linear RGB (CDN/WASM, sizeable) but full ACR-grade develop is a large build. Mark hard; lower priority than heal/inpaint for a browser suite.

features.feature: Frequency separation / dodge & burn / skin retouch tools
features.note: No dodge/burn brush, no frequency separation helper. Browser-only: dodge/burn = brush in screen/multiply blend on a 50% gray layer (S, reuses brush). Freq-sep = auto-build hi/lo layers via gaussianBlur (already have) + grain-extract blend (S-M). No model. Cheap pro credibility.

features.feature: HDR merge, focus stacking, panorama stitch
features.note: None present. Affinity markets these as no-plugin headline features. Browser-only feasible but heavy: pano = feature-match+homography (OpenCV.js, CDN WASM ~8-10MB); focus stack = per-pixel sharpness select (pure canvas, M); HDR merge+tonemap = exposure-weighted blend (pure canvas, M). OpenCV.js is the enabling CDN lib. L overall.

features.feature: Histogram + per-channel channels panel + on-canvas color sampler readout
features.note: No live histogram/channels view (we compute LUTs but never show distribution). Browser-only trivial: read composite ImageData, bin into 256, draw to a small canvas; channels = R/G/B/alpha isolate previews. S effort. No model. Expected by anyone doing levels/curves.

features.feature: Gradient tool (draw fg->bg / multi-stop gradient onto canvas, radial/linear/angle)
features.note: Gradient exists ONLY as a layer style overlay (layer-styles.ts), not as a paint tool you drag on the canvas. Browser-only: createLinearGradient/createRadialGradient driven by drag start/end onto active paint layer. S effort, fills an obvious table-stakes hole. No model.

features.feature: Smart guides, snapping, alignment, rulers, grid
features.note: ui.tsx has showRulers/showGrid + zoom/pan/fit, but rulers state is not rendered with tick marks and there is no snapping/align of layers to edges/centers/each other. Browser-only: edge/center snap on move (compare layer bbox to canvas + sibling bboxes), align/distribute buttons. S-M effort. No model.

features.feature: AI Generative Fill / Generative Expand / text-to-image (create new content)
features.note: Generative create (not just heal) is the marquee differentiator of 2026 rivals. HONESTLY out of on-device scope: a usable diffusion model is GBs, violates the <=180MB budget. Mark NOT feasible on-device. The achievable, honest substitute = content-aware INPAINT fill (MI-GAN, see above) for removal, plus 'expand' via edge-aware outpainting heuristic. Do not chase true gen-fill locally.

features.feature: Denoise + AI upscale (super-resolution)
features.note: No denoise/upscale. Feasible on-device: Real-ESRGAN x4 / x2 ONNX (~17-65MB depending on variant) via onnxruntime-web WebGPU, tiled to control memory; denoise via the same family or bilateral filter (pure canvas). needs-model, fits budget. High perceived quality win.

features.feature: Undo/redo with history panel; persistent project save/load; export PNG/JPG/WebP with quality
features.note: ui.tsx UndoStack(80) + HistoryList; newProject/saveProject/loadProject (IndexedDB); ExportDialog png/jpg/webp + quality, usage-gated.

features.feature: Batch processing (apply edit/recipe to many images)
features.note: Single-doc only. Xonvert has separate batch tools but Image Studio has no record-an-action-and-replay. Browser-only: record the commit() label stream as a macro, re-run over a folder of files. M effort. No model. (Separate batch tools may partially cover this elsewhere in the suite.)

features.feature: Layer/element animation (entrance / emphasis / exit) with preview
features.rival: Canva (limited), none of the pro raster editors
features.note: ui.tsx AnimationPanel + computeElementState + RAF preview loop. Unusual differentiator vs raster rivals (shared with Video Studio). Keep + lean into export-to-GIF/MP4.

features.feature: Export to animated GIF / WebP / MP4 from the animation timeline
features.note: Animation can PREVIEW but export is still a single still frame (exportImage uses composite). Since the suite already has a frame-accurate video compositor + ffmpeg.wasm noted in the codebase, wiring animated layers -> frames -> encoder is M effort and turns a preview gimmick into a real deliverable. No new model.

features.feature: 16-bit / HDR / CMYK color depth + ICC color management
features.note: All work is 8-bit sRGB Canvas2D ImageData. Matters for print/pro photo. Browser-only HARD: Canvas2D is 8-bit; 16-bit needs Float32 buffers + WebGL pipeline rewrite; CMYK/ICC needs a color-engine. Low priority for a browser-first social/creator tool; mark hard.

features.feature: EXIF/metadata read + preserve/strip on export
features.note: No EXIF read (orientation, camera) or strip-on-export control. Auto-orient especially matters (phone photos load sideways). Browser-only: exifr (CDN, tiny JS) to read + apply orientation on load; strip by re-encoding (already do). S effort. No model.

topGaps.title: Content-aware / AI object removal (brush-mask inpainting)
topGaps.approach: The defining 2025-26 feature on every web rival (Canva Magic Eraser, Pixlr/Picsart object remove, Figma Erase Object) and the top 'toy vs tool' differentiator. We already have brush+layer-mask plumbing (strokeAt/addMaskToLayer) — wire the painted mask as the inpaint mask. Load MI-GAN 512 ONNX (~20-30MB, the model open-source inpaint-web ships) or LaMa via onnxruntime-web with WebGPU fast path + WASM fallback; tile large images to cap memory. Fully on-device, well under 180MB. Reuse the existing removeBackgroundAuto loader pattern.

topGaps.title: Healing brush + clone stamp + dodge/burn retouch
topGaps.approach: Pure-canvas, no model — closes the biggest photo-retouch credibility gap. Clone stamp = Alt-set source offset, then brush draws sampled pixels at the offset (S). Spot/healing brush = copy a sampled patch and seamless-clone it (Poisson blend, or simpler: blur-match the patch's low frequencies to the target via the existing gaussianBlur) so texture transplants without a seam (M). Dodge/burn = brush painting white/black onto a 50%-gray screen/multiply layer (S, reuses brush engine). All slot into the existing tool dock + strokeAt.

topGaps.title: PSD import/export
topGaps.approach: PSD interop is Photopea's whole reason to exist and a pro interoperability must-have; as a browser tool it's a strong differentiator. Use ag-psd (pure-JS CDN lib, no model): read PSD -> map layers/masks/blend modes/text/adjustments onto our DocState (our model already has layers, masks, 16 blend modes, text, adjustment layers — close mapping), and write our DocState back out to .psd. Extends fileToCanvas/openImageFiles for read and adds a PSD branch to export.

topGaps.title: WebGL filter gallery + Liquify
topGaps.approach: Today filters are only 3x3 kernels + gaussian, which reads as a toy next to Affinity's Liquify Persona and Photoshop's distort gallery. Add glfx.js (WebGL, tiny) for swirl/bulge/pinch/lens-blur/triangle-blur/ink/vignette/hue-lens/perspective at GPU speed; build Liquify as a forward push/twirl/bloat/pucker mesh warp on a WebGL texture driven by brush drag. Big visual-wow per effort, no model, no server.

topGaps.title: Selection refine (feather/grow/contract/smooth) + boolean add/subtract + Select-Subject
topGaps.approach: Selections are the foundation of compositing and ours is replace-only with hard edges. Feather = gaussianBlur on the mask alpha (lib already has it); grow/contract = morphological dilate/erode; smooth = blur+threshold; add/subtract/intersect = Shift/Alt modifier compositing in onPointerUp. Select-Subject for ~free: run the existing removeBackgroundAuto matte and threshold its alpha into a SelectionPath.mask. Mostly reuses code already in the repo.

topGaps.title: Free Transform handles (scale/rotate/skew/distort/perspective)
topGaps.approach: ImageLayer already stores scaleX/scaleY/rotation and renderLayer applies them, and transformActive state exists but has no UI. Add an on-canvas bounding box with 8 scale handles + rotate handle + Ctrl-drag corner for skew/distort; perspective/distort corners via a 3x3 homography warp rendered through a small WebGL texture pass (or glfx.js perspective). No model. Turns the existing dead fields into a real, expected pro tool.

topGaps.title: Layer groups/folders + clipping masks
topGaps.approach: Real documents need organization; flat layers[] caps us. Add a 'group' layer kind whose children composite to an offscreen canvas then blend as one unit (honoring group opacity/blend/mask); clipping mask = clip a layer to the alpha of the one below via destination-in. Extends the existing compositeDoc loop and LayerRow tree. No model, no server.

topGaps.title: Gradient tool + histogram/channels panel + EXIF auto-orient
topGaps.approach: Three cheap table-stakes wins. Gradient tool: drag on the active paint layer with createLinear/RadialGradient (fg->bg, multi-stop) — gradient code already exists as a layer style, just expose it as a paint tool. Histogram/channels: read composite ImageData, bin 256 per channel, draw to a small canvas; channel isolate previews. EXIF: exifr (tiny CDN JS) to read orientation and rotate phone photos right-side-up on load + a strip-metadata export toggle. All pure browser, no model.

topGaps.title: AI denoise + super-resolution upscale
topGaps.approach: Pixlr/Picsart/Photoshop all upscale; high perceived-quality win. Real-ESRGAN x2/x4 ONNX (~17-65MB) via onnxruntime-web WebGPU, tiled to bound memory, reusing the on-device model loader pattern already used for background removal. Denoise via the same model family or a fast bilateral filter in pure canvas as the no-model fallback. Fits the <=180MB budget.

topGaps.title: Export animation to GIF/WebP/MP4
topGaps.approach: Layer animation currently only previews (export still flattens one frame), making it feel like a gimmick. The codebase already has a frame-accurate video compositor + ffmpeg.wasm; render the animation frames (computeElementState over time, which already drives the preview) into that encoder to emit GIF/animated-WebP/MP4. Converts an existing differentiator into a real shippable deliverable. No new model.

features.feature: Open / render PDF pages (page thumbnails, multi-page nav)
features.note: ui.tsx addPdf() rasterizes via engines/pdf/rasterize rasterizePdf (maxEdge 1200), page sidebar grid with PreviewCanvas thumbnails, select/nav. Fully there.

features.feature: Page organize: reorder, rotate, delete, duplicate
features.note: ui.tsx rotatePage/deletePage/duplicatePage/movePage all wired with undo; thumbnail hover actions + keyboard (left/right/delete).

features.feature: Split PDF (by range / every N pages)
features.note: lib/studios/pdf-mastery.ts splitPdf() + SplitDialog (every-N and custom ranges). Solid.

features.feature: Merge / combine multiple PDFs into one
features.note: Multi-file open in ui.tsx appends all pages into one working doc and Export emits a single combined PDF — so merge IS achievable, but there is no explicit 'Merge' action, no drag-combine of separate files, no inter-doc page interleaving UX. The single most-used web-PDF verb is hidden. Trivial to surface.

features.feature: Compress / reduce file size (quality tiers)
features.note: pdf-mastery.ts compressPdf() light/balanced/strong rasterize+re-embed JPEG with useObjectStreams, keeps smaller of {orig,compressed}. Honest tradeoff (flattens vector text) shown in export dialog. Good — but image-only path; no lossless object/stream optimization for vector PDFs.

features.feature: Annotate: highlight, freehand draw, shapes (rect/ellipse/line), text box, image stamp
features.note: ui.tsx tools + engines/pdf/studio.ts drawAnnotation render all of these to real pdf-lib vector ops (drawText/drawLine/drawEllipse/drawRectangle/drawImage). Annotations are normalized 0..1 so resolution-independent.

features.feature: Text/sticky-note comments + review threads (reply, resolve, author colors)
features.note: ui.tsx CommentsModel/CommentsThread/CommentsOverviewPanel — threaded comments, replies, resolve/unresolve, per-author color (pickPeerColor), jump-to. Stronger than most web tools. Caveat: anchor is page-level (page-rect 0,0,1,1), not point-anchored to a spot/word.

features.feature: Hand-drawn signature capture + place on page
features.note: ui.tsx SignatureDialog (pointer canvas, trimToContent auto-crop) → places PNG via 'sign' tool. Works.

features.feature: Page numbers / headers / footers
features.note: ui.tsx pageNumbers checkbox → studio.ts drawPageNumber (centered 'n / total' only). No custom header/footer text, no left/right positioning, no date/filename tokens, no Bates. Sejda/Acrobat have full header-footer with tokens.

features.feature: Watermark (text + image, opacity/rotation/position)
features.note: pdf-mastery.ts applyWatermarkToPdf + WatermarkDialog (text/color/opacity/size/rotation/5 positions). Image watermark supported in engine (imageBytes) though dialog only exposes text.

features.feature: OCR scanned page → extractable text (multi-language)
features.rival: Acrobat, Foxit, PDF Expert, Sejda, Smallpdf
features.note: ui.tsx runOcr() via lib/studios ocrCanvas + OCR_LANGUAGES selector (Tesseract.js under the hood). Per-page extract-to-clipboard dialog.

features.feature: Make searchable PDF (OCR → invisible text layer over scan)
features.note: pdf-mastery.ts makeSearchablePdf() rasterizes, OCRs each page, lays render-mode-3 invisible word-positioned text over the image. Real searchable-PDF output.

features.feature: True redaction (content permanently destroyed, not just covered)
features.rival: Acrobat, Foxit (Smart Redact 99% PII), PDF Expert
features.note: studio.ts destructive redaction path: rasterizes the page, burns black boxes into pixels, re-embeds as flat image so underlying text is physically gone; then RE-OCRs survivors into an invisible layer (skipping boxes that overlap a redaction). This is genuinely best-in-class for a browser tool and matches Acrobat's flatten-on-apply behavior.

features.feature: Auto / smart redact (find PII: emails, phones, SSNs)
features.note: ui.tsx runSmartRedact() uses pdf.js getTextContent + findPii (regex) to auto-place redaction boxes on the CURRENT page only. Strong start but: (a) single-page not whole-doc, (b) regex-only PII (no names/addresses NER), (c) no pattern/keyword search-and-redact, (d) misses text inside images. Foxit claims 99% via AI.

features.feature: Auto-deskew tilted scan
features.note: ui.tsx runAutoDeskew() → lib/studios deskewCanvas detects angle and rotates raster. Nice extra most web tools lack.

features.feature: PDF → Word (.docx) export
features.note: pdf-mastery.ts pdfToDocx() extracts text with pdf.js then dumps paragraphs into ooxml exportDocx. It is text-only: NO layout, tables, columns, images, fonts, or styling preserved — far below iLovePDF/Smallpdf/Acrobat which reconstruct layout. Functional but feels toy on real documents.

features.feature: PDF → Excel / PowerPoint / structured data
features.note: No PDF→xlsx/pptx. Matters: every web rival ships these as core verbs. Browser-feasible: table detection from pdf.js text-item geometry → SheetJS (xlsx) and a pptx writer (pptxgenjs); we already have ooxml/JSZip. No model needed.

features.feature: PDF → images (JPG/PNG per page) export
features.note: We rasterize every page to canvas already (rasterizePdf); there is NO 'export pages as images' action. Trivial: canvas.toBlob loop + zip. Currently missing as a user verb.

features.feature: Images / Office → PDF (create PDF from JPG/Word/etc.)
features.note: Studio only opens existing PDFs. No image-to-PDF or office-to-PDF entry. Browser-feasible: image→PDF is pdf-lib drawImage on blank pages (we have blankCanvas); office→PDF can reuse existing converter tools. Matters as the on-ramp for users with no PDF yet.

features.feature: Edit EXISTING text in the PDF (true content editing, reflow)
features.rival: Acrobat, Foxit (Word-level reflow + Link&Join), PDF Expert, Sejda
features.note: BIGGEST GAP. Our 'text' tool only OVERLAYS new text via window.prompt (ui.tsx onEditorDown). You cannot click existing text, fix a typo, change a number, or reflow a paragraph. This is THE feature that separates an 'editor' from an 'annotator' and is exactly why it feels like a toy. Feasible browser-only at the line/run level: pdf.js gives per-item text+transform+font+width; rebuild as editable boxes, redraw with pdf-lib embedded font, white-box the original run. Hard for full reflow but achievable for single-line/value edits (Sejda-style). No model needed.

features.feature: Interactive form FILLING (AcroForm/XFA fields)
features.note: We never read a PDF's existing AcroForm. pdf-lib exposes form.getFields()/getTextField().setText()/checkbox.check() — fillable forms could be detected, rendered as real HTML inputs over the page, and written back as filled values. Currently a user with a tax/government form cannot fill it. Browser-feasible, no model.

features.feature: Interactive form CREATION (add real fields: text/checkbox/radio/dropdown/signature)
features.note: pdf-mastery.ts applyFormFieldsToPdf DRAWS static visuals (boxes, a painted ✓, 'Sign here') — they are NOT interactive AcroForm widgets, and formFields state in ui.tsx is never populated by any UI (no field tool wired). To be real: pdf-lib form.createTextField/createCheckBox + addToPage. Feasible, no model.

features.feature: Compare two PDFs (visual + text diff, change list)
features.note: No compare. Matters for legal/contract review. Browser-feasible: text diff via pdf.js getTextContent + a diff lib (diff-match-patch from CDN), plus pixel-diff of rasters side-by-side highlighting changed regions. No model needed.

features.feature: Password protect / encrypt (open password + permissions)
features.note: encryptPdfWithMetadata in pdf-mastery.ts is a FACADE — it only edits Title/Subject metadata and stamps a footer; it performs NO actual encryption (pdf-lib cannot encrypt). Claiming 'password-protected' is misleading. Real browser encryption needs a CDN lib: pdfcpu-wasm or qpdf-wasm (AES-256), or HummusJS/muhammara is server-only. Feasible with WASM lib <=180MB; also need DECRYPT (open password-protected PDFs — currently addPdf just fails).

features.feature: Digital / certificate signature (cryptographic, verifiable PKCS#7)
features.note: We only stamp a drawn-image signature (cosmetic). No cryptographic signing, no certificate, no validation. Acrobat/Foxit do PKCS#7 detached + LTV. Feasible-ish browser-only: WebCrypto + a PAdES library (pdf-lib + @signpdf/signpdf style) using a user-supplied .p12; complex but no server/model. Niche but it's the 'legally binding' bar.

features.feature: Bates numbering (legal sequential stamps across docs)
features.note: drawPageNumber only does centered 'n / total'. Bates = prefix + zero-padded sequence + suffix at a chosen corner, continuing across a batch. Trivial extension of existing footer code. No model. Cheap legal-credibility win.

features.feature: Flatten (make annotations/form fields non-editable, baked-in)
features.note: Export already bakes our overlay annotations into the page content (and redaction flattens to raster), so output is effectively flattened. But there is no explicit 'Flatten form fields' for an INCOMING PDF's interactive fields (we never read them), and no user-facing flatten verb.

features.feature: Crop pages / resize page box / change page size
features.note: Rotate only; no crop, no margin/page-size adjust. Browser-feasible with pdf-lib setMediaBox/setCropBox + a crop-rect UI on the canvas. No model.

features.feature: Extract pages / extract single pages to new files
features.note: Split covers contiguous ranges; no 'select arbitrary pages → extract' or 'delete selected pages → save'. delete-page exists in editor but there is no multi-select extract verb. Easy via existing copyPages.

features.feature: Edit / view document metadata (title, author, keywords)
features.note: pdf-lib setTitle/setAuthor/setSubject/setKeywords available; no UI. Sejda has a dedicated metadata editor. Tiny build, no model.

features.feature: Hyperlinks / bookmarks (outline) / internal navigation editing
features.note: No link tool, no bookmark/outline editor. pdf-lib can add link annotations and an outline (lower-level). Medium effort, no model. Matters for long-doc usability.

features.feature: Accessibility: tags, reading order, alt text, PDF/UA check
features.note: No tagging/structure. This is a deep Acrobat moat (WCAG/PDF/UA remediation). Hard browser-only (requires structure tree authoring); low priority for a creative suite but worth noting as a pro gap.

features.feature: PDF/A archival conversion + preflight/standards compliance
features.note: No PDF/A export or preflight. Partly feasible: pdf-lib can embed fonts + set OutputIntent/XMP for a basic PDF/A-ish save, but true PDF/A-1b/2b validation needs veraPDF (heavy/server). Mark hard browser-only. Niche.

features.feature: AI assistant: chat with PDF / summarize / translate document
features.rival: Acrobat AI Assistant, Smallpdf (Chat+Translate), PDF Expert Copilot, Foxit AI
features.note: No AI in the studio. This is the 2025-2026 marquee differentiator across ALL rivals. We already have an on-device AI stack (SmolLM2/SmolVLM, oioxo brain, <=180MB models per project memory) and extractPdfText — wiring 'summarize this PDF / ask a question / translate' on-device is highly differentiated (fully private, no upload) and directly reusable. Feasible with existing on-device models; this is the single highest-marketing-value miss.

features.feature: Point/word-anchored annotations & precise text-markup (underline, strikethrough over real text)
features.rival: Acrobat, Foxit, PDF Expert (highlight/underline/strikethrough on selected text)
features.note: We have a rectangle-drag highlight and freehand, but NO text-selection-based highlight/underline/strikethrough (select the actual words → mark them). pdf.js text layer gives selectable runs to anchor marks. Medium effort, no model. Real readers expect this.

topGaps.title: Edit existing PDF text (click-to-fix-a-line, font-matched)
topGaps.approach: This is the #1 reason it feels like a toy. Use pdf.js getTextContent() to get per-item str + transform (position, scale, rotation) + fontName + width. On click, hit-test the item, render an inline contentEditable box over it pre-filled with the run text. On commit: white-box the original run's bbox (reuse the redaction/whiteout flatten ONLY over that rect, or paint a matched-background rect) and draw replacement text with pdf-lib using an embedded font sized to match (map base14 + embed via fontkit for non-Helvetica via @pdf-lib/fontkit, already pdf-lib-compatible). Ship line/value editing first (Sejda parity); full paragraph reflow is XL and optional. No model, no server.

topGaps.title: Chat-with-PDF / summarize / translate, fully on-device
topGaps.approach: Highest marketing leverage and the one feature every rival now leads with — but ours is the ONLY private one (no upload). We already have extractPdfText (pdf.js) and the on-device AI stack (SmolLM2-360M / SmolVLM, oioxo brain, <=180MB, per project memory). Wire: extract text per page → chunk → feed the existing on-device chat/summarize/translate pipeline behind a 'Ask AI' panel in the studio. Cite page numbers for grounding (reuse the engine's grounded-read pattern). Reuses models already in budget; near-zero new download. Differentiator: 'AI that never sees the cloud.'

topGaps.title: Surface MERGE as a first-class verb + arbitrary page extract/delete-to-new-file
topGaps.approach: The plumbing exists (multi-open already concatenates into one Export; copyPages already used by splitPdf). Add a 'Combine files' action (drop multiple PDFs, order them, one combined export) and a page multi-select → 'Extract selected' / 'Delete selected & save'. Pure UI + reuse of pdf-lib copyPages. Closes the most-used web-PDF verbs (iLovePDF/Smallpdf flagship) for almost no cost.

topGaps.title: Real interactive form fill + form creation (AcroForm)
topGaps.approach: Two parts. FILL: on open, pdf-lib form.getFields() → overlay real HTML inputs/checkboxes positioned from each field's widget rect; write back with setText()/check() and flatten-or-keep on export. CREATE: add a 'field' tool (text/checkbox/radio/dropdown/signature) that calls form.createTextField/createCheckBox/createDropdown + field.addToPage — replacing the current applyFormFieldsToPdf which only PAINTS fake widgets. No model. Unlocks the entire tax/gov/HR form use case we currently can't serve.

topGaps.title: Real password protection + open encrypted PDFs (AES)
topGaps.approach: Stop shipping the encryptPdfWithMetadata facade (it only sets metadata — misleading). pdf-lib can't encrypt, so load a WASM crypto lib from CDN: pdfcpu-wasm or qpdf-wasm (both AES-256, well under 180MB) for set-user/owner-password + permissions, AND to DECRYPT password-protected PDFs on open (today addPdf just fails with 'may be password-protected'). Self-host only the limits per project rules; load the WASM from official CDN. Table-stakes everyone has.

topGaps.title: PDF → Excel / PowerPoint / per-page images (export verbs)
topGaps.approach: PDF→images: trivial — we already rasterize every page; add canvas.toBlob loop → JSZip download (PNG/JPG, per-page or zip). PDF→Excel: detect tables from pdf.js text-item geometry (cluster by x/y into rows/cols) → SheetJS (xlsx) write; we already use ooxml/JSZip. PDF→PPT: one slide per page via pptxgenjs (CDN) with extracted text + page raster as background. Also upgrade pdfToDocx beyond a flat text dump (group runs into lines/paragraphs, keep images). No model; closes the converter verbs every web rival ships.

topGaps.title: Whole-document smart redact + search-and-redact + NER names/addresses
topGaps.approach: Extend runSmartRedact from current-page-only to ALL pages, add 'find a word/pattern → redact every occurrence' (Acrobat's Find&Redact), and add a redaction-mark review step before destructive flatten. Upgrade PII beyond regex: a tiny on-device NER (SmolVLM/SmolLM prompt or a small token-classifier <=180MB) for names/addresses/account numbers that regex misses — closing toward Foxit's 99% PII claim while staying fully on-device.

topGaps.title: Text-selection markup (highlight/underline/strikethrough on real words) + point-anchored comments
topGaps.approach: Render the pdf.js text layer over the canvas so users can SELECT actual words, then attach highlight/underline/strikethrough annotations to those run rects (real reader behavior, currently only rectangle-drag highlight). Anchor comments to the selected run/point instead of the whole page (CommentsModel already supports anchors). No model; makes annotation feel professional rather than toy.

topGaps.title: Compare two PDFs (text + visual diff with change list)
topGaps.approach: Text diff: pdf.js getTextContent on both → diff-match-patch (CDN) → list inserted/deleted/changed runs, jump-to. Visual diff: pixel-diff the two page rasters (we already rasterize) and highlight changed regions in a side-by-side view. A real legal/contract-review feature only Acrobat/Foxit have; fully browser-only.

topGaps.title: Headers/footers with tokens + Bates numbering + crop + metadata editor (pro polish bundle)
topGaps.approach: Low-cost credibility cluster on existing code. Headers/footers: extend drawPageNumber to left/center/right slots with tokens ({page},{pages},{date},{filename}) + custom text. Bates: prefix + zero-padded counter + suffix, continuing across batch. Crop: pdf-lib setCropBox/setMediaBox driven by a canvas crop-rect. Metadata: pdf-lib setTitle/Author/Subject/Keywords behind a small panel. All pdf-lib, no model, mostly small additions.

features.feature: Step sequencer / drum grid (16-step, multi-lane)
features.rival: FL Studio (Channel Rack), GarageBand (Beat Sequencer), Soundtrap (Patterns Beatmaker), BandLab
features.note: ui.tsx SequencerGrid: 16-step grid x 8 lanes (kick/snare/hihat/clap drums + bass/lead/pad/pluck synths), right-click cycles synth pitch 0-7, swing, per-step play head. Solid and on par with a beatmaker grid — but locked to 16 steps and 8 fixed instruments.

features.feature: Pattern chaining into a song / arrangement
features.note: ui.tsx DocState.chain + loopChain lets you order patterns into a song and loop. But it's a linear pattern queue, not a free arrangement timeline with per-track clip placement, drag-resize, or markers. Rivals all have a true timeline.

features.feature: Per-track volume / pan / mute / solo mixer
features.note: ui.tsx Mix sidebar + Instrument {volume,pan,muted,solo}; playback honors solo/mute live (togglePlay reads docRef). Pan applied via StereoPanner per track. No fader metering/dB readout or sends/buses.

features.feature: Master bus EQ / compressor / limiter / reverb / delay chain
features.note: effect-presets.ts (16 effects) + audio-master-chain.ts builds a real Web Audio node chain: 3-band EQ (peaking mid), DynamicsCompressor, brickwall limiter, ConvolverNode reverb (4 IR sizes), feedback delay, de-ess, stereo widener. KEY STRENGTH: buildMasterChain is mounted in BOTH live AudioContext and OfflineAudioContext so preview == export exactly. This is genuinely pro-grade, not a toy.

features.feature: Real DSP primitives (RBJ biquads, WSOLA stretch, FF compressor, Freeverb)
features.note: dsp.ts: RBJ Audio-EQ-Cookbook shelving biquads, WSOLA time-stretch with similarity search (pitch-preserving), pitchShift (stretch+resample), feed-forward peak compressor with attack/release ballistics, downward gate, Schroeder/Freeverb (parallel combs + series allpass). Honest, correctly-implemented — not fake static-gain effects.

features.feature: BS.1770 / LUFS integrated loudness + true-peak normalize
features.note: loudness.ts: full ITU-R BS.1770-4 K-weighting (re-derived per sample rate), 400ms/75%-overlap blocks, absolute -70 + relative -10 two-stage gate, 4x true-peak estimate, normalizeLoudness to target (-16/-23) with true-peak ceiling. This BEATS most web rivals which peak-normalize. A real differentiator already present.

features.feature: Tempo / key / swing / BPM controls
features.note: ui.tsx top bar: BPM 40-240, Key (12 keys), Swing 0-70%, master gain. Swing offset applied to odd steps in both playback and export.

features.feature: Procedural song / genre generation
features.note: engines/music/studio.ts generateSong: 6 genres (lofi/house/hiphop/ambient/pop/synthwave), music-theory chord progressions, seeded RNG, bass/lead/pad/drums. Plus humanize, chord-fill, randomize in ui.tsx. No model, fully on-device. Comparable in spirit to SongStarter but pattern-grid output, not full arrangement.

features.feature: Audio-to-MIDI transcription
features.note: ui.tsx importAudioFile -> audioBufferToMidi (lib/studios) detects notes, shows table, imports to Lead lane, exports .mid. But it's monophonic pitch detection (single lane, % 8 pitch folding on import) — not polyphonic. BandLab does polyphonic per-stem. Feasible to upgrade with a CREPE/basic-pitch ONNX model (<25MB).

features.feature: WAV + MP3 export
features.note: engines/audio/index.ts encodeWav (RIFF) + encodeMp3 (@breezystack/lamejs, worker-offloaded). Export renders through the same master chain offline. Free sessions get brand metadata. No FLAC/OGG/stems export.

features.feature: Save / load projects, undo/redo, keyboard shortcuts
features.note: ui.tsx UndoStack(80) + commit pattern, saveProject/loadProject library (IndexedDB via lib/studios), full shortcut map (space/mod+s/e/o/z, +/- BPM). Good editor hygiene.

features.feature: MIDI piano roll editor (draw/move/resize notes, velocity, length)
features.rival: FL Studio, Logic, Soundtrap, Soundation, GarageBand, BandLab
features.note: We only have a fixed 16-step grid with 8 pitch rows (ROW_PITCHES) and right-click pitch cycling — NOT a piano roll. Every single rival has a real piano roll with variable note length, velocity, glide, and a full keyboard range. This is THE biggest table-stakes gap that makes it feel like a toy. Fully feasible browser-only (SVG/canvas grid + Web Audio scheduling); no model needed.

features.feature: Record / import your own audio onto a timeline track
features.rival: Audacity, all DAWs, BandLab, Soundtrap, GarageBand
features.note: importAudioFile only runs audio->MIDI; there is no audio track you can drop a vocal/guitar take onto and arrange. No mic recording (getUserMedia + MediaRecorder). This is core to every rival. Feasible browser-only: getUserMedia capture, decodeAudioData import, draw waveform, schedule via AudioBufferSourceNode. No model.

features.feature: Real sampled instruments / SoundFont (SF2) playback
features.rival: GarageBand, Soundtrap, Soundation, BandLab, Logic, FL
features.note: All instruments are raw oscillator/noise synths (scheduleKick/Synth in ui.tsx) — they sound synthetic, a core reason it feels like a toy. Rivals ship real recorded instruments. Feasible browser-only: spessasynth/sf2-based playback or small curated SF2 banks loaded from CDN; a single GM-lite SF2 is ~2-30MB. Could also load drum one-shots. No proprietary model needed.

features.feature: Automation lanes (volume/pan/filter/effect params over time)
features.rival: FL (automation clips), Ableton, Logic, Soundtrap 2.0 (automate every effect), Soundation
features.note: No parameter automation at all — everything is static per pattern. Soundtrap explicitly markets 'automate every effect' as its biggest leap. Feasible browser-only: store breakpoint envelopes, apply via AudioParam.setValueCurveAtTime / linearRampToValueAtTime in the scheduler. No model, medium UI work.

features.feature: AI stem separation (vocals/drums/bass/other)
features.rival: BandLab Splitter (2/4/7 stems), Moises, Logic Stem Splitter
features.note: engines/audio/index.ts removeVocals/isolateVocals do center-channel cancellation only (mid/side) — honestly labeled 'not true stem separation'. Real per-instrument stems are missing. FEASIBLE browser-only: SCNet ONNX is 44.5MB FP32 / 22.6MB FP16 (well under 180MB), runs via onnxruntime-web WASM/WebGPU at ~3x realtime; Demucs-v4 ONNX also runs in-browser. This is a flagship-grade killer feature within budget.

features.feature: Pitch correction / Auto-Tune / vocal tuning
features.rival: BandLab AutoPitch, Soundtrap (Antares Auto-Tune), Logic Flex Pitch, GarageBand
features.note: No pitch correction. We have WSOLA pitchShift (dsp.ts) for a fixed shift but no pitch-tracking + snap-to-scale tuner. Feasible browser-only: YIN/pYIN pitch tracking (pure JS) + our existing pitchShift to retune to nearest scale note; the hard-tune effect is a real differentiator and needs NO model. Medium effort.

features.feature: Loop / sample library (royalty-free loops, one-shots)
features.rival: Soundtrap (24k loops), GarageBand, BandLab, Soundation (20k), FL, Logic (Apple Loops)
features.note: Zero loop/sample content — only synthesized hits. A curated tempo/key-tagged loop pack is a major creative on-ramp every rival has. Feasible browser-only but is a CONTENT problem (license + host small CC0 packs on CDN, time-stretch to project tempo via our WSOLA). No model; content/legal is the cost.

features.feature: Per-track / per-clip insert effects (not just master)
features.note: EffectsRack is only on the master bus (ui.tsx mounts one rack). You can't put a filter on just the hi-hats or reverb on just the lead. Feasible browser-only: reuse buildMasterChain per-track in the scheduler (build a chain per instrument trackGain). Medium effort, no model — the chain infra already exists.

features.feature: Spectral / spectrogram view + surgical spectral editing
features.rival: Audacity (spectral edit multitool, notch, spectral delete)
features.note: No spectrogram or frequency-domain editing. Audacity's spectral editing is a signature pro feature for surgical noise/click removal. Feasible browser-only: FFT (pure JS or WebGPU) to render a spectrogram canvas + STFT masking for spectral delete. Larger effort; niche vs piano roll but high-credibility.

features.feature: Noise reduction / audio restoration (learn noise profile)
features.note: engines/audio/denoise.ts runs RNNoise (@shiguredo/rnnoise-wasm) — real on-device suppression, but tuned for SPEECH and not surfaced in the Music Studio UI (no button calls denoise() here). Audacity's spectral-subtraction 'learn a noise profile from a selection' workflow is missing. Surfacing denoise + adding profile-based reduction is low effort.

features.feature: Comping (take lanes, multi-take record + best-bits comp)
features.rival: Ableton Live 12 (take lanes), Logic (quick swipe comping)
features.note: We don't record audio at all, so no comping. Depends on the audio-recording gap above. Lower priority until recording exists; feasible browser-only afterward.

features.feature: Clip launcher / Live-Loops grid (non-linear performance)
features.rival: Ableton Session View, GarageBand Live Loops
features.note: We have linear pattern chaining only. A Session/Live-Loops grid (trigger cells/scenes live, quantized launch) is a signature creative feature. Feasible browser-only: quantized clip-launch scheduling on top of the existing pattern model + a cell grid UI. Medium effort, no model.

features.feature: MIDI hardware / computer-keyboard live input + recording
features.rival: all (Web MIDI in web rivals; GarageBand touch)
features.note: No Web MIDI API input and no computer-keyboard piano. You can only click the grid. Feasible browser-only: navigator.requestMIDIAccess + a QWERTY keyboard map driving scheduleSynth; record into the piano roll. Low/medium effort, no model.

features.feature: Real-time collaboration (multi-user same project)
features.note: Single-user only. The web rivals' #1 differentiator is live co-editing. Hard to do truly server-less, but the suite already has P2P (WebRTC /send, /chat) infra per project memory — a CRDT-over-WebRTC session is feasible without a compute server (signaling only). Large effort; flagship-level payoff.

features.feature: One-click AI mastering presets
features.note: We have all the building blocks (EQ/comp/limiter chain + true BS.1770 loudness normalize in loudness.ts) but no one-click 'master to streaming-loud' preset that analyzes the mix and dials the chain. Feasible browser-only NOW with our own code: measure LUFS + spectral tilt, auto-set EQ/comp/limiter to a target, normalize to -14 LUFS. Low effort, high perceived value, NO model.

features.feature: Variable pattern length / time signatures
features.note: newPattern is hardcoded to 16 steps (ui.tsx); Pattern.steps exists in the type so the grid is length-aware, but there's no UI to change it and no non-4/4 meters. Feasible browser-only, low effort (expose steps, support 8/12/24/32/3-4 etc).

features.feature: Real-time meters (peak/RMS/LUFS, spectrum analyzer)
features.note: loudness.ts measures LUFS offline and project memory references a lufs-meter.ts, but the Music Studio UI shows NO live meter, spectrum, or correlation display. Feasible browser-only: AnalyserNode for spectrum + a live LUFS meter. Low effort.

topGaps.title: Replace the 8x16 grid with a real MIDI piano roll + variable-length clips
topGaps.approach: This is the single biggest reason it reads as a toy: every rival (FL/Logic/Soundtrap/Soundation/GarageBand/BandLab) has a piano roll and we have a fixed 16-step, 8-pitch grid. Build a canvas/SVG piano-roll component (full keyboard range, draw/drag/resize notes, per-note velocity + length, snap/quantize, marquee select). Replace DocState patterns' fixed ROW_PITCHES note model with {pitch, start, length, velocity} note objects; the scheduler in togglePlay/exportNow already iterates notes and calls scheduleSynth(freq,dur,vol) so it adapts cleanly. Keep the drum step-grid as one view mode. No model, pure Web Audio + DOM.

topGaps.title: On-device AI stem separation (vocals/drums/bass/other) — flagship killer
topGaps.approach: Replace the honest-but-weak center-channel removeVocals/isolateVocals with real ML separation. Ship SCNet ONNX (44.5MB FP32 / 22.6MB FP16 — well under the 180MB budget) or a quantized Demucs-v4, run via onnxruntime-web (WASM+SIMD, WebGPU when available) in a worker; ~3x realtime, ~18s for a 51s song with threads. Output 2/4 stems as new tracks (free=2 stem, Pro=4+), exportable as WAV. Pairs with stem export and stem->MIDI. This is BandLab Splitter parity, fully on-device, and a genuine 'best in the world for browser' claim.

topGaps.title: Real recorded instruments + drum kits via SoundFont (SF2) playback
topGaps.approach: The oscillator-only synths (scheduleKick/scheduleSynth) are the other big 'toy' tell. Add an SF2 sampler path: load a small GM-lite SoundFont (curated ~5-30MB) from CDN and render notes with spessasynth or a lightweight SF2 player, selectable per instrument. Provide a handful of real drum-kit one-shot banks (CC0). Keep synths as an option. Note model contract is unchanged (freq+dur+vel), so the scheduler just routes to a sampler instead of an oscillator. Content/license is the main cost, not engineering.

topGaps.title: Mic + file recording onto real audio tracks (then comping)
topGaps.approach: Add audio tracks alongside the instrument lanes: getUserMedia + MediaRecorder/ScriptProcessor capture, decodeAudioData for imports, render a waveform, schedule playback via AudioBufferSourceNode through the (per-track) effect chain, trim/move on the timeline. This unlocks vocals/guitar over the beat — the core loop of BandLab/Soundtrap/GarageBand — and is a prerequisite for comping and pitch correction. Pure Web Audio, no model. Pairs with the arrangement-timeline upgrade.

topGaps.title: One-click AI Master (analyze mix -> auto EQ/comp/limiter -> -14 LUFS)
topGaps.approach: Highest ROI per effort: we already have the entire chain (audio-master-chain.ts) AND true BS.1770 loudness (loudness.ts). Add a 'Master' button that renders the mix, measures integrated LUFS + spectral tilt (AnalyserNode/FFT), then auto-populates masterEffects (corrective 3-band EQ, gentle compressor, limiter) and runs normalizeLoudness to -14/-16 with a -1 dBTP ceiling. Offer Fire/Clarity/Tape-style presets like BandLab. Matches a marquee web-rival feature with code we already own, zero model.

topGaps.title: Per-track insert effects + parameter automation lanes
topGaps.approach: Two related gaps. (1) Per-track FX: the EffectsRack is master-only; reuse buildMasterChain per instrument by inserting a chain between each trackGain and the master in the scheduler (already builds per-step trackGain nodes). (2) Automation: store breakpoint envelopes per param and apply with AudioParam.linearRampToValueAtTime/setValueCurveAtTime during scheduling and offline export. Soundtrap markets 'automate every effect' as its biggest leap; this closes it. No model.

topGaps.title: Pitch correction / Auto-Tune to scale
topGaps.approach: Once audio tracks exist, add vocal tuning: YIN/pYIN pitch tracking (pure JS, no model) to get the f0 contour, snap to nearest note in the project key/scale, retune with our existing WSOLA pitchShift (dsp.ts) per-segment, with a 'retune speed' (hard/natural) and formant-preserve option. Matches BandLab AutoPitch / Soundtrap Antares. Pure DSP, no model — a strong differentiator for a browser tool.

topGaps.title: Live meters: spectrum analyzer + LUFS/peak/RMS on the master
topGaps.approach: Cheap credibility win. Add an AnalyserNode on the master output for a real-time spectrum + level meters, and a running LUFS meter (project memory references lib/studios/lufs-meter.ts — surface it). Sits in the existing right sidebar next to the Master chain. No model; makes the loudness work we already did visible and makes the studio feel professional.

features.feature: Multitrack timeline with clip trim/split/move/duplicate, snap, zoom
features.note: ui.tsx Timeline component + splitClip/duplicateClip/onTrimClip/onMoveClip; 4 default tracks (V1-3 + Music), snappedT, zoom 20-400px/s. Solid, frame-of-reference editor.

features.feature: Per-track mute / solo / lock / volume / pan
features.note: ui.tsx onTrackToggle (muted/solo/locked), onTrackVolume, onTrackPan; StereoPanner + GainNode per track in startPlayback/exportNow.

features.feature: Mic recording with echo-cancel / noise-suppress / AGC
features.note: ui.tsx startRecording: getUserMedia({echoCancellation,noiseSuppression,autoGainControl}) + MediaRecorder. Note: browser-grade DSP, not the AI studio-sound rivals ship.

features.feature: Import common formats (WAV/MP3/M4A/OGG/FLAC) + WAV/MP3 export
features.note: ui.tsx importFiles regex + audio.decode; exportNow renders 48k stereo via OfflineAudioContext → encodeWav/encodeMp3(192).

features.feature: Undo/redo history, project save/load
features.note: ui.tsx UndoStack(80) + commit/undo/redo; saveProject/loadProject. Caveat: save persists doc only — audio buffers are NOT stored, user must re-import (toast says so). Real projects don't lose their media.

features.feature: Fades (in/out), gain, normalize per clip
features.note: ClipInspector fadeIn/fadeOut/gainDb/normalized → applyChain uses audio.fadeIn/fadeOut/gain/normalize.

features.feature: EQ (bass/treble + 3-band), compressor, limiter, noise-gate, reverb, delay, stereo widener, de-ess, pitch shift, pitch-preserving time-stretch
features.note: EffectsRack + applyEffectChain (ui.tsx) and buildMasterChain (audio-master-chain.ts): real DynamicsCompressor, brickwall limiter, mid/side widener, ConvolverNode reverb, feedback delay; changeTempo (WSOLA) keeps pitch. Genuinely pro-grade signal path.

features.feature: BS.1770 LUFS + true-peak metering and loudness normalize to target (−16 LUFS)
features.note: LufsMeter/LufsMeterDisplay live during playback; exportNow → audio.loudnessNormalize(final,-16,-1). This is a real differentiator vs the web/mobile TTS rivals which have none.

features.feature: Spectrogram view
features.note: SpectrogramView renders the selected clip (ui.tsx sidebar) — VIEW only. RX's whole product is editing ON the spectrogram (paint-select, attenuate, repair). We display, we can't edit it.

features.feature: Auto-remove silences / dead-air trim
features.note: removeSilencesFromClip → findSilences(-38dB, 0.35s) splits the clip into kept segments. Matches Riverside 'Set Pace'/silence trim.

features.feature: One-click broadcast/podcast mastering preset
features.note: applyBroadcastPreset → broadcastChain(normalizeLUFS:-16) sets gain/bass/treble/normalize/fades. Honest, lightweight mastering.

features.feature: On-device text-to-speech, many languages, multiple voices
features.note: engines/tts/studio.ts: MMS-TTS (1100+ langs, 20 surfaced) fully on-device, free, private. BUT only 6 voices and they are DSP playback-rate/ring-mod derivatives of ONE neutral model (robot/cartoon/deep) — not the 200-800 natural human voices or emotion/style control rivals ship. Quality + expressiveness gap is the core 'feels like a toy' complaint.

features.feature: Transcription / speech-to-text with timestamps
features.note: WE ALREADY SHIP THIS ELSEWHERE but Voice Studio doesn't use it: engines/transcribe/index.ts = Whisper tiny(~40MB)/base/small(~150MB) on-device, word/sentence timestamps, 99 langs, multi-threaded WASM. Not imported by ui.tsx. This is the single biggest unlock — it gates text-based editing, filler removal, captions, search.

features.feature: Text-based editing (edit transcript → audio follows; delete a word deletes the audio)
features.note: The defining feature of the modern category and absent. Feasible browser-only on top of the Whisper word-timestamps we already have: map each transcript token to a [start,end] span on the clip, deleting a token = splice that source range (reuse the splitClip/segment logic in removeSilencesFromClip). No model beyond Whisper.

features.feature: AI filler-word removal (um/uh/like, one click)
features.note: Why it matters: top-3 reason creators choose Descript/Riverside. Feasible once transcription is wired: regex/dictionary match on transcript tokens (um, uh, like, you know) → splice their timestamp ranges, same engine as remove-silences. No extra model. Effort small after ASR is in.

features.feature: AI voice enhancement / studio-sound (denoise + de-reverb + clarity, one click)
features.rival: Adobe Podcast Enhance Speech v2, Descript Studio Sound, RX
features.note: THE flagship feature of Adobe Podcast and a Descript headliner — turns phone/cafe audio into studio quality. We only have browser getUserMedia NS during capture, nothing for imported audio. Feasible on-device with a speech-enhancement ONNX model under 180MB: DeepFilterNet3 (~ a few MB, ONNX, runs real-time in WASM) or a GTCRN/DTLN denoiser. This is the highest-impact gap for the 'best in the world' bar.

features.feature: Background-music / source separation (isolate vocals from music)
features.note: RX Dialogue Isolate / Music Rebalance separate voice from noise+music with sliders. Feasible but heavy: an ONNX UMX/Demucs-lite or a 2-stem MDX model — smallest usable 2-stem models (~30-60MB int8) fit 180MB but are slow in WASM (acceptable for an offline 'process' action). Lower priority than denoise; denoise covers most podcast pain.

features.feature: Speaker diarization / auto speaker labels on multi-person recordings
features.note: lib/studios/diarization.ts EXISTS (energy + spectral-centroid k-means, 1-3 speakers) but is DEAD CODE — imported nowhere except the barrel. Wiring it (color clips/segments by speaker A/B/C) is small. Honest caveat: centroid-clustering is far weaker than embedding-based diarization; good enough for a v1 label, not for overlapping speakers.

features.feature: Instant voice cloning (clone the user's own voice from a short sample, then TTS in it)
features.note: The marquee feature of every web/mobile rival. Honestly NOT feasible at our bar today: quality voice cloning + TTS (XTTS-v2, StyleTTS2, etc.) is >180MB and/or needs server GPU. Document as a deliberate non-goal; do not fake it. Partial alternative: more + better-quality stock voices (see TTS row).

features.feature: Voice changer (convert a recording into a different target voice, keep timing)
features.note: Needs a voice-conversion model (RVC/so-vits) typically >180MB and GPU-grade. Not feasible on-device at quality. Our 6 DSP 'styles' (pitch/ring-mod) are a toy version and shouldn't be marketed as a voice changer.

features.feature: Auto dubbing / translate speech to another language preserving voice
features.note: We have the 3 pieces separately (Whisper transcribe+translate in engines/transcribe with task:'translate', on-device translate lib, MMS-TTS) but they are not chained and voice-preservation needs cloning (infeasible). A 'translate + re-narrate in a stock voice' chain IS feasible on-device and would be a genuine differentiator even without voice preservation.

features.feature: Auto-generated short/social clips from highlights (Magic Clips)
features.note: Audio-only relevance is lower, but exporting transcript-selected ranges as clips is trivial once text-based editing exists. Defer; video studio is the better home.

features.feature: Spectral repair / paint-out a sound (cough, click, beep) on the spectrogram
features.note: RX's signature. We render a spectrogram (read-only) but can't select/attenuate regions. Feasible browser-only as a DSP feature (STFT → mask painted region → ISTFT) — no model, but L effort and a niche pro audience. Lower leverage than denoise/text-edit for a podcast/voiceover tool.

features.feature: De-click / de-hum / de-plosive targeted repair
features.note: We have de-ess (high-shelf approximation per audio-master-chain comment, not a true dynamic sidechain) and a noise gate. No de-click/de-hum/de-plosive. De-hum (notch at 50/60Hz + harmonics) and de-click (median/transient detect) are feasible browser-only DSP, no model. Medium effort, pro-tier polish.

features.feature: Per-clip / pause / pronunciation / emphasis control on synthesized speech (SSML-style)
features.note: Rivals give word-level emphasis, pause insertion, phoneme pronunciation overrides. MMS-TTS has no SSML, but we can fake the useful subset on-device: insert silence for pauses, post-DSP gain bump for emphasis, and per-word respeak. Medium effort, only matters once TTS quality itself improves.

features.feature: Captions / subtitle export (SRT/VTT) from the voiceover
features.note: Engines already exist: engines/transcribe chunksToSrt/chunksToVtt. Trivial to surface in Voice Studio once ASR is wired — an export option. Small effort, high creator value.

features.feature: Real-time effect preview == export (WYSIWYG master chain)
