features.note: audio-master-chain.ts buildMasterChain is mounted in BOTH the realtime AudioContext and the export OfflineAudioContext so preview equals output by construction. Genuine engineering strength worth keeping.

topGaps.title: Wire the Whisper ASR we already ship into Voice Studio (transcript panel + word timestamps)
topGaps.approach: Import engines/transcribe (transcribe + audioToWhisperInput) — already on-device Whisper tiny~40MB/small~150MB, multi-threaded WASM, word timestamps via return_timestamps:'word'. Add a 'Transcribe clip' action and a transcript panel; store {token,start,end} per clip. This is the foundation for text-based edit, filler removal, diarization labels, and SRT export. The code exists; it's purely an integration.

topGaps.title: On-device AI voice enhancement (denoise + de-reverb 'Studio Sound' button)
topGaps.approach: Ship a speech-enhancement ONNX model under budget — DeepFilterNet3 (a few MB, designed for real-time, runs in WASM) or DTLN/GTCRN denoiser; run the imported/recorded buffer through it via onnxruntime-web, output a cleaned buffer (same pattern as applyDeEss). This closes the Adobe Podcast / Descript Studio-Sound gap that most defines 'pro vs toy' for spoken audio. Load model lazily and gate behind the usage policy like other heavy actions.

topGaps.title: Text-based editing: delete/move words in the transcript → splice the audio
topGaps.approach: On top of Whisper word timestamps, render the transcript as editable tokens; map each token to a source [start,end] range. Deleting tokens computes kept ranges and rebuilds clip segments exactly like removeSilencesFromClip already does (it splices ranges into new clips). No new model. This is the single feature that puts us in Descript/Riverside's category.

topGaps.title: One-click filler-word + silence cleanup driven by the transcript
topGaps.approach: After ASR, scan tokens against a per-language filler dictionary (um, uh, er, like, you know) and splice their timestamp ranges using the same segment-rebuild path as remove-silences; combine with the existing findSilences pass into one 'Clean up' button. Small once ASR + range-splice exist.

topGaps.title: Wire the existing diarization into clip/segment speaker labels
topGaps.approach: diarization.ts (diarizeAudio) is finished but dead. Call it on a recording, color/segment the timeline by speaker A/B/C, and feed speaker turns into the transcript view. Be honest in copy that it's centroid-based (good for clearly different voices, weak on overlap). Cheap, visible, distinguishing.

topGaps.title: Caption/subtitle export (SRT/VTT) + improve TTS voice count/quality
topGaps.approach: SRT/VTT: surface engines/transcribe chunksToSrt/chunksToVtt as an export option — trivial. TTS quality (the literal 'toy' feeling): the 6 voices are DSP rate-shifts of one MMS model. Add real distinct voices by loading additional small per-speaker TTS checkpoints where they fit under 180MB, and add pause/emphasis post-processing; manage expectations vs ElevenLabs but materially raise the floor.

topGaps.title: Persist audio buffers in saved projects (fix re-import-required save)
topGaps.approach: saveCurrent stores only the doc; users must re-import media on open (toast admits it). Store decoded buffers as encoded WAV/Opus blobs in IndexedDB keyed by bufferKey (project.ts already has an IDB layer) and rehydrate on load. A 'real' studio doesn't drop your audio on save — table-stakes credibility fix.

group: Office Studios (docs / slides / sheets / diagram / chart)

features.feature: Basic inline formatting (bold/italic/underline, H1-H2, bullet/number lists, L/C/R align, hyperlink)
features.note: tools/studio-docs/ui.tsx cmd() wraps document.execCommand bold/italic/underline/formatBlock H1-H2/insertUnordered+OrderedList/justifyLeft-Center-Right/createLink. Real but uses the deprecated execCommand API.

features.feature: Font family, font size, text color, highlight, strikethrough, sub/superscript
features.note: No font/size/color/highlight controls in ui.tsx toolbar at all. Every rival has these as the baseline. Feasible browser-only: execCommand fontName/fontSize/foreColor/hiliteColor or a Selection+span wrap; trivial, no lib.

features.feature: Tables (insert, resize, merge cells, borders)
features.note: No table insertion in ui.tsx. Critical table-stakes — a word processor without tables reads as a toy. Feasible browser-only: contentEditable <table> insertion + column resize handles; no lib needed, though export fidelity needs work.

features.feature: Insert images / drag-drop image, wrap text, resize
features.note: No image insertion path. Feasible browser-only: FileReader -> dataURL into contentEditable, or insertImage execCommand; resize via CSS handles. No lib.

features.feature: DOCX export preserving formatting
features.note: exportDocx() in ui.tsx calls textToDocx(ref.current.innerText) (engines/doc/docx-write.ts) which takes innerText and emits one bare <w:p> per line — ALL bold/headings/lists/links/tables are LOST. So DOCX 'export' is plain text only. Fix: walk the HTML DOM -> OOXML runs (rPr b/i/u, pStyle Heading, numbering). M effort, browser-only, no lib.

features.feature: DOCX import with formatting
features.note: importFile() in ui.tsx uses docxToHtml() (engines/document/index.ts -> mammoth.convertToHtml) then sanitizeHtml into contentEditable. Real, on-device. Mammoth drops some styling (colors, exact fonts) but bold/headings/lists/links survive.

features.feature: PDF export
features.note: exportPdf() -> htmlToPdf() (engines/document/index.ts) renders via jsPDF.html + html2canvas at scale 0.72, A4, autoPaging text. Rasterized layout, watermarked for free via brandJsPdf. Works.

features.feature: Find & replace
features.note: No find/replace. Universal expectation. Feasible browser-only: Range search over text nodes + replace; or window.find for highlight. S effort, no lib.

features.feature: Word/character count, reading stats
features.note: No counters. Trivial: count innerText tokens live. S effort, no lib.

features.feature: Spell check
features.note: contentEditable has spellCheck attribute set in ui.tsx (line 124). Relies on native browser spellcheck — acceptable; grammar is not present.

features.feature: Page setup (size, margins, orientation), headers/footers, page numbers, columns
features.note: Editor is a single fixed 820px 'page' div; no page model, no headers/footers/columns/page numbers. Feasible but real layout work: a paged-media layout (CSS @page emulation) or paginate.js-style chunking. L effort.

features.feature: Comments / track changes / suggesting mode
features.note: No comments or revision tracking. Matters for any review workflow. Feasible browser-only single-user: store ranges + before/after deltas; render strike+insert. Multi-user needs P2P (you have WebRTC Send/chat infra). M effort single-user.

features.feature: Real-time multiplayer co-editing with cursors
features.note: No collaboration. The single biggest gap vs Google Docs. Feasible browser-only WITHOUT a server: Yjs (yjs + y-webrtc, CDN) over your existing WebRTC signaling -> CRDT shared doc, live cursors via awareness. Differentiator: 'real-time co-editing, no account, no server'. L effort, with-cdn-lib (yjs ~70KB).

features.feature: Styles / outline / table of contents / document structure nav
features.note: No style system or outline pane. Feasible: derive outline from H1/H2 nodes (you already produce them) -> clickable nav + auto-TOC insertion. S-M effort, no lib.

features.feature: On-device AI writing assist (draft/rewrite/summarize/translate)
features.rival: Word Copilot, Google Docs Gemini, Notion AI, Canva Magic Write
features.note: No AI in studio-docs/ui.tsx itself, BUT the repo has an on-device <=180MB writer/conductor stack (lib/ai/*, SmolLM2/conductor on HF) used by oioxo search. Wiring a 'rewrite/summarize selection' button to the existing in-browser model is the killer move rivals charge for. M effort, needs-model (already in budget).

features.feature: Multiple slides: add/duplicate/delete/reorder
features.note: studio-slides/ui.tsx addSlide/dupSlide/delSlide/move(-1|1) with a thumbnail rail. Solid.

features.feature: Themes / templates
features.note: 5 hard-coded THEMES (Paper/Midnight/Ink/Forest/Berry) in ui.tsx — color swap only, single layout (title + accent bar + body). No real templates (title/section/two-column/comparison layouts). Rivals ship hundreds. Adding a layouts enum + template gallery is M effort, no lib.

features.feature: Free placement of text boxes, images, shapes on a slide
features.note: Each slide is exactly ONE title textarea + ONE body textarea (ui.tsx editor). No element model, no images, no shapes, no drag positioning. This is THE reason it feels like a toy — every rival is a free canvas. Feasible browser-only: an element array {type,x,y,w,h,...} on a positioned canvas (you already do this in studio-diagram). L effort, no lib.

features.feature: Insert images / icons / media
features.note: No image support. Feasible: FileReader -> element; canvas paint already draws text, add drawImage. Tied to the element-model rework. M effort.

features.feature: Speaker notes
features.note: No notes field on the Slide interface. Trivial: add notes string + a notes pane; export to PDF notes pages. S effort.

features.feature: Presenter / present mode (fullscreen, next-slide, timer, notes)
features.note: No present mode — you can only export. Feasible browser-only: Fullscreen API + keyboard nav over the existing paint(); presenter view via a second window. S-M effort, no lib.

features.feature: Slide transitions & element animations
features.rival: PowerPoint (incl. Morph), Google Slides, Canva (Magic Animate)
features.note: No transitions/animations. Feasible browser-only with CSS/Web Animations API; Morph-style is matching elements between slides + FLIP tween (you have the element ids once you build the element model). M effort, no lib. PowerPoint Morph is the marquee feature here.

features.feature: PPTX import & export
features.note: Only PDF deck + PNG slide export (ui.tsx exportPdf/exportPng); no .pptx in or out. Feasible browser-only: PptxGenJS (CDN) for export; import via JSZip + OOXML parse (harder). Export is M effort with-cdn-lib (PptxGenJS); import is L.

features.feature: AI deck generation from a prompt/outline/doc
features.rival: Canva Magic Design, PowerPoint Copilot, Gemini in Slides
features.note: No generation. Feasible on-device: existing writer model produces an outline -> map to template layouts (once element model + templates exist). High differentiator: 'generate a deck offline, free'. L effort, needs-model (in budget).

features.feature: Real-time co-editing
features.note: Same Yjs-over-WebRTC approach as docs. L effort, with-cdn-lib.

features.feature: PDF deck / PNG slide export
features.note: exportPdf() builds a landscape jsPDF deck mirroring the canvas paint; exportPng() exports current slide. Watermark-aware (brandJsPdf). Works but exports only the title+body layout.

features.feature: Editable grid, add rows/cols, formula bar, active-cell
features.note: studio-sheets/ui.tsx: 40x12 grid, sticky headers, formula bar bound to active cell, add Rows/Cols buttons. Solid baseline.

features.feature: Formula engine with cell refs & ranges
features.note: makeEvaluator() supports SUM/AVERAGE/MIN/MAX/COUNT/PRODUCT/ROUND/ABS + arithmetic, A1:B9 ranges, cycle detection (#CYCLE). Real and safe (Function() guarded by /^[-+*/().\d\s]*$/). But that's 8 functions vs Excel's 450+ — no IF/AND/OR, VLOOKUP/XLOOKUP/INDEX-MATCH, COUNTIF/SUMIF, IFERROR, CONCAT/LEFT/RIGHT/MID, dates, %, $ refs, multi-cell array spill.

features.feature: Logical/lookup/text/date functions (IF, VLOOKUP, COUNTIF, etc.)
features.note: None present (switch in evalExpr only has the 8 math fns). This is the core of a spreadsheet. Feasible browser-only: extend the evaluator OR swap to HyperFormula (CDN, MIT, ~Excel-compatible 390+ fns, supports strings/dates/booleans). HyperFormula is the high-leverage drop-in. M effort with-cdn-lib.

features.feature: Cell formatting (number/currency/date formats, fonts, fill, borders, align)
features.note: Cells are raw <input>; no per-cell format/style state, no number formatting. Every rival has this. Feasible: extend cell model to {value,fmt,style}; SheetJS export supports cell styles via the pro build but basic styles are doable. M effort.

features.feature: Sort & filter, freeze panes
features.note: Header row is CSS-sticky only (not a user freeze); no sort, no autofilter. Feasible browser-only on the in-memory model. S-M effort, no lib.

features.feature: Conditional formatting (color scales, data bars, icon sets, rules)
features.note: Absent. Feasible: rule set over the cell model rendered as inline styles/mini-bars (Excel does data bars as cell backgrounds). M effort, no lib.

features.feature: Multiple sheets / tabs
features.note: Single sheet only (load() reads wb.SheetNames[0]; export writes one 'Sheet1'). Feasible: sheets array + tab bar; SheetJS already round-trips multiple sheets. M effort.

features.feature: Charts embedded from sheet data
features.note: No in-sheet charting — though studio-chart exists separately. Feasible: reuse studio-chart's drawChart over a selected range -> overlay element. M effort, no lib (own code).

features.feature: Pivot tables
features.note: Absent. Feasible browser-only: group-by aggregation over the cell model -> output range; or pivottable.js (CDN). M-L effort, with-cdn-lib optional.

features.feature: Data validation / dropdowns
features.note: No validation rules. Feasible: per-cell/column rule -> <select> or guarded input. M effort, no lib.

features.feature: XLSX / CSV import & export
features.note: load() XLSX.read; exportAs xlsx/csv via SheetJS (studio-sheets/ui.tsx). On-device, deferred-revoke for mobile. Solid (values only — no styles round-tripped).

features.feature: Undo/redo
features.note: No undo stack anywhere in the suite (all five studios lack it). Feasible: snapshot/command history on the state objects. M effort, applies to all five.

features.feature: Place nodes, drag to move, delete
features.note: studio-diagram/ui.tsx: addNode, pointer drag with clamping, del; SVG viewBox 1000x620. Real and touch-aware (touch-none, setPointerCapture).

features.feature: Connect nodes with arrows
features.note: Link mode connects source->target with a straight <line> + arrowhead marker (onNodeDown). But: straight center-to-center only (line passes UNDER boxes), no edge labels, no curved/orthogonal routing, no anchor ports. Real but crude.

features.feature: Shape library / multiple node shapes (diamond, circle, cylinder, etc.)
features.note: Only one shape: a rounded rect (svgMarkup hardcodes <rect rx=10>). Flowcharts need decision diamonds, terminators, etc. Feasible browser-only: a shape-type enum -> SVG path per type; no lib. S-M effort. Visio/Lucidchart ship thousands of stencils (UML/BPMN/network/AWS).

features.feature: Orthogonal/smart connector routing that avoids shapes + edge labels
features.note: Straight lines only, no routing, no labels. Feasible browser-only: anchor on box edges + Manhattan routing; or adopt a layout lib. M effort, no lib for basic ortho.

features.feature: Auto-layout (tree/hierarchy/force) & diagram-from-text
features.note: Manual placement only. Feasible browser-only: dagre or elkjs (CDN) for hierarchical auto-layout; mermaid (CDN) for text->diagram (mermaid renders flowchart/sequence/ER/gantt/class from markdown). mermaid is a huge fast win and a differentiator on-device. M effort with-cdn-lib (mermaid/dagre).

features.feature: Diagram type templates: flowchart/UML/BPMN/ERD/org chart/mind map/swimlanes/network
features.note: No types/templates — it's a generic box-and-line canvas. Feasible: starter templates + shape sets per type; mermaid covers UML/ER/sequence/class/gantt/state out of the box. M-L effort, with-cdn-lib.

features.feature: Node text styling, grouping, layers, multi-select, resize handles
features.note: Single-select only; fixed font/size; fixed node size (NW=150 NH=60); no resize, no group, no z-order. Feasible browser-only, all own code. M effort.

features.feature: Sticky notes / freehand / infinite pannable+zoomable canvas
features.note: Fixed 1000x620 viewBox, no pan/zoom, no stickies, no freehand. Whiteboard rivals are built on this. Feasible browser-only: SVG/canvas pan-zoom transform + pointer freehand path + sticky element type. M-L effort, no lib (or use a CDN canvas lib).

features.feature: PNG / SVG export
features.note: downloadSvg (brandSvg watermark) + downloadPng (SVG->Image->canvas). Policy-gated via enforcePolicy. Works; PNG is at fixed 1000x620 (no hi-DPI scale).

features.feature: Data-linked shapes (bind to Sheets/CSV, auto-update)
features.note: Absent. Feasible browser-only: import CSV (you have SheetJS) -> generate/refresh nodes from rows. M effort, reuse existing lib.

features.feature: Core chart types: bar/line/area/pie
features.note: studio-chart/ui.tsx drawChart renders bar (grouped multi-series), line, area, pie with legend + gridlines + y-axis labels on canvas; buildSvg mirrors to vector. Solid for the four types.

features.feature: CSV/paste data input, multi-series, header detection
features.note: parseData() auto-detects header row, supports N series from columns; live preview via useMemo+useEffect. Good.

features.feature: Extended chart types: scatter, bubble, stacked/100% bar, combo, donut, radar, histogram, box, treemap, waterfall, gauge
features.note: Only bar/line/area/pie. Rivals ship 15-30+ types. Scatter/stacked/donut/combo are baseline expectations. Feasible: extend drawChart, or adopt Chart.js (CDN, MIT) which gives all these + tooltips/legends free. M effort with-cdn-lib (Chart.js).

features.feature: Axis titles, data labels, custom colors/legend position, gridline control
features.note: Hard-coded PALETTE, no axis titles, no value labels on points/bars, no legend placement, no color picker. Only chart title + type are configurable. Feasible: own code, or free via Chart.js options. S-M effort.

features.feature: Interactive chart (hover tooltips, click-legend toggle, zoom)
features.note: Static canvas render only — no interactivity. Feasible: Chart.js gives tooltips/legend toggle out of the box; or own hit-testing. M effort with-cdn-lib.

features.feature: PNG / SVG export
features.note: downloadPng (canvas.toDataURL) + downloadSvg (brandSvg(buildSvg)), policy-gated with rows lever. Works. Note: buildSvg omits axes/gridlines/legend that the canvas has (vector is simplified).

features.feature: Live chart bound to spreadsheet data (auto-refresh)
features.note: Chart is fed by pasted CSV, not bound to studio-sheets. Feasible browser-only: share a data store / pass a sheet range into the chart. M effort, own code — also closes the sheets 'embedded chart' gap.

topGaps.title: Free-canvas element model (text boxes + images + shapes, drag/resize/z-order)
topGaps.approach: Replace the single title+body textarea per Slide with an elements array [{id,type:'text'|'image'|'shape',x,y,w,h,style,content}] rendered on an absolutely-positioned slide stage with drag/resize handles — exactly the pattern studio-diagram already uses for nodes. paint() and the jsPDF deck loop then iterate elements instead of two fields. This single change is what flips Slides from 'toy' to real and unblocks images, animations, AI generation and PPTX export. Browser-only, no lib.

topGaps.title: Real formula engine via HyperFormula (IF/VLOOKUP/COUNTIF/dates/text, 390+ fns)
topGaps.approach: Swap the hand-rolled makeEvaluator (8 math fns, numbers only) for HyperFormula (MIT, CDN, Excel-grammar compatible, supports strings/booleans/dates/array spill). Keep the existing grid + formula bar UI; feed cell map in, read computed values out. Closes the biggest credibility gap (a spreadsheet that can't do IF/VLOOKUP isn't a spreadsheet). Add multi-sheet tabs and cell number-formatting alongside (SheetJS already round-trips both).

topGaps.title: Format-preserving DOCX export (HTML DOM -> OOXML runs)
topGaps.approach: exportDocx currently dumps innerText -> every bold/heading/list/link/table is silently lost (engines/doc/docx-write.ts). Walk the contentEditable DOM and emit OOXML: <w:r><w:rPr><w:b/></w:rPr>..</w:r> for bold/italic/underline, w:pStyle Heading1/2, <w:numPr> for lists, hyperlink rels, and a w:tbl for tables. Browser-only, JSZip already used. Restores trust in 'export to Word'. Pair with adding font/size/color + tables + images to the editor toolbar (all execCommand/contentEditable, S each).

topGaps.title: Text-to-diagram + auto-layout via mermaid (and dagre/elkjs)
topGaps.approach: Add a mermaid (CDN, MIT) path: type a flowchart/sequence/ER/class/gantt/mindmap in markdown -> rendered SVG, instantly giving UML/BPMN-ish/ERD/org/mind-map coverage that Visio/Lucidchart charge for. For the hand-drawn canvas, add dagre or elkjs (CDN) auto-layout + a shape-type enum (diamond/circle/cylinder/terminator) and orthogonal edge routing with edge labels. On-device, no server — 'diagram from text, offline' is a real differentiator.

topGaps.title: Server-free real-time co-editing across docs/slides/sheets (Yjs over WebRTC)
topGaps.approach: Add Yjs (yjs + y-webrtc, CDN, ~70KB) as a shared CRDT layer over the existing WebRTC signaling already powering Xonvert Send/chat/call. Bind the doc/slide/cell models to a Y.Doc; render peer cursors via the awareness protocol. Marketed as 'real-time co-editing with live cursors — no account, no server, fully on-device' it beats Google Docs on the privacy/cost axis. Apply once, reuse across all studios.

topGaps.title: Chart.js drop-in for chart types + interactivity + axis/labels
topGaps.approach: Adopt Chart.js (CDN, MIT) behind the existing CSV parser + type picker to add scatter/bubble/stacked/100%/combo/donut/radar/histogram, axis titles, data labels, custom colors, legend placement, and hover tooltips/legend-toggle interactivity in one move (drawChart currently hand-renders only 4 static types). Keep the existing canvas/SVG export by exporting the Chart.js canvas. Also bind it to a studio-sheets range to close the 'embedded live chart' gap in both studios.

topGaps.title: Present mode + speaker notes + PPTX export
topGaps.approach: (a) Present mode: Fullscreen API + arrow-key nav over the existing paint(), plus a presenter window (notes/next-slide/timer). (b) Add a notes:string to the Slide interface + notes pane. (c) PPTX export via PptxGenJS (CDN, MIT) iterating the new element model so decks open in PowerPoint/Keynote/Slides — today export is PDF/PNG only. All browser-only.

topGaps.title: On-device AI writing/diagram/deck assist (reuse the existing <=180MB model)
topGaps.approach: The repo already ships an on-device writer/conductor (lib/ai/*, SmolLM2/conductor, within the 180MB budget) for oioxo search. Wire 'Rewrite / Summarize / Translate selection' into studio-docs, 'Generate deck from prompt/outline' into studio-slides (maps to the new template layouts), and 'diagram from description' into studio-diagram. Rivals (Copilot/Gemini/Magic/Notion AI) gate this behind paid cloud; doing it free + offline is a flagship differentiator.

topGaps.title: Conditional formatting + sort/filter + data validation
topGaps.approach: Extend the cell model to {value,fmt,style}. Add a rules layer for conditional formatting (color scales, data bars as cell-background gradients, icon sets), column sort + autofilter over the in-memory model, and per-column data validation (dropdown via <select>). All browser-only, no lib; raises Sheets from a value grid to an actual analysis surface.

topGaps.title: Infinite pan/zoom canvas + sticky notes + freehand (Miro/FigJam parity)
topGaps.approach: Add a viewBox transform driven by wheel-zoom + space-drag pan, a sticky-note element type, and pointer-based freehand path capture. This moves studio-diagram from 'fixed flowchart frame' toward the whiteboard category (Miro/FigJam) where infinite canvas + stickies + freehand are table-stakes. Browser-only; combine with multi-select + grouping + node resize handles for a complete editing model.

topGaps.title: Universal undo/redo across all five studios
topGaps.approach: None of the five studios has undo/redo today — a glaring 'toy' tell. Add a generic command/snapshot history hook (debounced state snapshots or command objects) and wire Ctrl+Z/Ctrl+Y in docs/slides/sheets/diagram/chart. Browser-only, shared utility.

features.note: runTranscribe wires @/engines/transcribe (Whisper tiny/base/small) with language select, runs locally, ui.tsx:307-337. Genuinely on-device which most web rivals are not.

features.rival: Subtitle Edit, Aegisub, Premiere, Veed, Kapwing

features.feature: Reading-speed (CPS/WPM) validation + warnings

features.note: runDiarization via @/lib/studios diarizeAudio, labelCuesWithSpeakers prefixes [A]/[B], ui.tsx:252-280. Energy/clustering-based, no rename UI but functional.

features.note: SUBTITLE_STYLES across 6 categories, full font/size/color/weight/outline/box/position controls, ui.tsx:758-819. Strong preset breadth.

features.note: CuePreview renders active cue with CSS text-stroke/shadow/box over the <video>, ui.tsx:697-699,886-914. WYSIWYG-ish but CSS-approx, not the burn-in renderer.

features.note: cuesToSrt/Vtt/Ass/json, ui.tsx:466-479. Covers the big 3 + json, but Subtitle Edit reads/writes ~200 formats (SBV, TTML/DFXP, SCC/CEA-608, STL, SAMI, CSV). No TTML/SCC = blocks broadcast/YouTube-pro workflows.

features.feature: Subtitle translation in-app

features.note: THE signature 2025 social-caption look. features.rival: Veed, Kapwing, CapCut, Happy Scribe (MP4), Premiere

features.feature: Transcript-mode editing (edit flowing text, timing follows)

features.note: No spell-check. Matters for delivery quality. Feasible browser-only: contentEditable spellcheck attr (free) or hunspell.wasm + dictionaries (<5MB/lang) via CDN for an in-panel checker.

features.feature: Auto emoji insertion based on caption context

features.note: ASS export is style-line only, strips formatting; no override-tag editing, no syllable splitter. Matters for anime/fansub niche. Feasible browser-only (pure string/timing work) but niche audience — lower priority than word-highlight.

features.note: runText → engines/doctranslate translateText (real on-device MT, language auto-detect), editable output box, ui.tsx:62-71. Truly offline — a differentiator vs cloud rivals.

features.note: Boxes are single-line whiteSpace:nowrap with one color/bg/size (ui.tsx:245, flatten shrinks-to-fit one line, :131-133). No wrapping, bold/italic, alignment, or font choice. Feasible browser-only canvas text layout work.

features.feature: Batch / multi-image or multi-page translation in one session
features.note: Single image at a time (loadImage resets state). Multi-page PDFs punted to a separate /tools/doc-translate (ui.tsx:187). Feasible browser-only: queue files, reuse prepareImageEditor per page.

topGaps.title: Burn-in / hard-sub video export (styled + animated captions baked onto video)
topGaps.approach: Composite each frame: drive playback with lib/studios/webcodecs-player.ts (WebCodecsPlayer + blitFrameToCanvas), draw the active cue using the same CuePreview style math onto an OffscreenCanvas, encode via WebCodecs VideoEncoder muxed with mp4-muxer (CDN) — fall back to ffmpeg.wasm (already a dep) for audio mux / unsupported codecs. This is the #1 'feels like a toy' fix: today the studio cannot produce a captioned video at all, only sidecar text.

topGaps.title: Word-level karaoke highlighting (the signature 2025 caption look)
topGaps.approach: Flip wordTimestamps:true in runTranscribe (engine already returns per-word times, engines/transcribe:156), store word offsets on each Cue, render the active word with a CSS highlight in CuePreview, and emit \k/\kf tags on ASS export. Pure UI + data plumbing, no new model. Pairs with the burn-in pass to bake the effect into video.

topGaps.title: Animated caption presets (pop-on, typewriter, bounce, glow, slide-up)
topGaps.approach: Reuse lib/studios/animation-presets.ts + keyframes.ts; map presets to CSS keyframes/transition timing driven off cue (and word) start times in CuePreview, then sample into the burn-in renderer. Add a preset gallery alongside the existing style presets. Directly closes the CapCut/Veed differentiator.

topGaps.title: Unify on-device subtitle/video translation across both studios
topGaps.approach: Replace subtitle-studio translateAll's Translator-API-only path (ui.tsx:410-435) with engines/doctranslate translateAll (the real on-device MT already powering translate-studio), and let translate-studio accept SRT/VTT/ASS files. Produces guaranteed-offline translated subs + optional bilingual cues. Removes the embarrassing 'translation unavailable on this device' dead-end and gives one coherent translate pipeline.

topGaps.title: Broadcast/web export formats: TTML/DFXP, SCC/CEA-608, SBV, plus min-gap/duration/line-length profiles (Netflix/EBU)
topGaps.approach: Add serializers for TTML, SCC, SBV next to cuesToSrt/Vtt/Ass, and a compliance auto-fixer (min duration, min gap, max 2 lines / 42 chars, CPS clamp) with selectable Netflix/EBU/YouTube profiles. Pure string + cue-logic, no deps. Converts 'toy' perception to 'pro-credible' for delivery pipelines that Subtitle Edit owns today.

topGaps.title: Transcript-mode editing with click-to-seek and word sync
topGaps.approach: Once word timestamps are stored, render a flowing document view (contentEditable) where clicking a word seeks the player and edits flow back into cues; enable native spellcheck on it for free. Matches Premiere/Happy Scribe long-form editing speed. UI-only.

topGaps.title: OCR image-based / hardcoded subtitles into editable cues
topGaps.approach: Sample video frames on an interval, run engines/ocr (Tesseract, already present) on the caption-safe lower third, dedupe consecutive identical reads into timed cues. Tesseract langdata pulled from CDN per language. Lets users recover/repair burned-in subs — a Subtitle Edit pro feature, on-device.

topGaps.title: Glossary / do-not-translate terms + bilingual output
topGaps.approach: A small term-map (source→locked target or never-translate) applied as pre/post substitution around translateAll, plus a 'keep original + translation' export toggle (stacked lines for subs, side-by-side for docs). Cheap, high consistency value for branded/character-name content.

topGaps.title: Auto-emoji insertion from caption context
topGaps.approach: Keyword→emoji lexicon (no model) inserting a context emoji per cue with a size/placement toggle, matching Veed Auto Emoji. Optionally upgrade to a tiny on-device intent classifier later. Low effort, strong social-creator appeal.

features.feature: Add/move/resize arbitrary text boxes (not just top/bottom)

features.feature: Caption-above (white space band) layout

features.feature: Animated GIF / video meme output
features.note: PNG only. Kapwing was first to do video memes; Imgflip has a GIF maker. Feasible browser-only for GIF via gif.js (CDN) and for short MP4 via WebCodecs/ffmpeg.wasm (already in the suite per memory). Effort L.

features.feature: Font choice, color, outline thickness controls

features.feature: Layered canvas with text/shape/image layers

features.note: Pointer-capture drag on overlay (lines 278-293, 640-668).

Feasible: ship a curated set of open fonts via FontFace from a CDN (e.g. Fontsource/Google Fonts files), await document.fonts.load before render. Effort M.

features.feature: Resize/rotate handles + element scaling on canvas
features.note: Position is draggable, but width/height are number-input only (no on-canvas resize handles) and there is no rotation at all (no rotation field on any layer). Add bounding-box handles + a rotation prop to renderCanvas (ctx.rotate). Effort M.

features.feature: Layer order controls (bring forward/back), opacity on text, lock

features.feature: Print sizes (A4/A3/Letter) + bleed + CMYK/PDF export
features.note: Canvas is fixed 600x850 px, PNG-only export. Posters/flyers are a PRINT product — rivals export print-ready PDF with bleed. features.feature: Curved / arced text, text-on-path
features.note: Only straight centered fillText. Adobe Express shipped curved text in 2025; expected on posters/logos. Feasible browser-only: render glyphs along an arc/path with canvas transforms per character. Effort M.

features.feature: Designed starter template gallery (100s)
features.note: Only 2 INITIAL_TEMPLATES (lines 54-193). Pure content expansion. Effort S per batch.

features.feature: Snap-to-grid / alignment guides / distribute

features.feature: 1280x720 canvas, big outlined auto-wrapped title
features.note: studio-thumbnail/ui.tsx: W=1280 H=720, word-wrap title with heavy black stroke + drop shadow, position top/center/bottom, size slider, font choice from 5 fonts, subtitle, corner badge (render lines 37-74).

features.feature: Photo OR gradient background + darken overlay

features.feature: Multiple text blocks, emoji/arrow/sticker overlays, draggable
features.note: Only one title + one subtitle, both fixed-centered; no draggable text, no arrows/circles/emoji stickers that define clickbait thumbnails. Reuse poster layer engine. Effort M.

features.feature: Platform aspect presets (Shorts 9:16, podcast, etc.)

features.feature: Styled QR: solid/gradient modules, palettes, center logo, EC levels, PNG+SVG

features.feature: Multiple content types (URL/text/Wi-Fi)

features.feature: Custom module shapes + eye (finder) styles

features.feature: Decorative frames with call-to-action ('SCAN ME')

features.feature: Editable education & skills sections (add/remove) in UI

features.feature: Cover-letter builder + JSON/save-resume / import

features.feature: Device frames (iPhone/Android/MacBook/iPad bezels) around a screenshot

features.feature: GIF maker: frames/video → GIF, trim, speed, caption, optimize

topGaps.title: Make resume PDF real selectable text + add ATS lint/score
topGaps.approach: Replace the html2canvas→jsPDF.addImage rasterization (studio-resume/ui.tsx lines 63-72) with real text layout via pdf-lib or @react-pdf/renderer (or jsPDF text API): every section becomes drawText with embedded fonts, so the PDF is parseable. Then add an on-device ATS lint (no model): check section presence, length, contact info, bullet verbs, keyword coverage vs a pasted job description, and emit a 0-100 score like Zety's checker.

topGaps.title: Bundled meme template gallery + N draggable text boxes + font/color
topGaps.approach: Meme tools live or die on the template library and flexible captions. Add a searchable grid of bundled blank templates (own/public-domain assets in JSON+thumbnails — no model), let users add/drag/resize multiple text boxes (lift the layer+drag model straight from studio-poster startDrag/onBoxMove), and expose font family, color, stroke width. topGaps.title: Real font library + on-canvas resize/rotate handles + alignment guides
topGaps.approach: The hardcoded 'sans-serif' (poster renderCanvas line 348) is the #1 'toy' tell. Ship a curated set of open fonts loaded via FontFace from a CDN (Fontsource/Google Fonts files added to CSP), await document.fonts.ready before render. Add a rotation prop + bounding-box resize handles to the drag overlay (ctx.translate/rotate/scale in render), and snap-to-edge/center alignment guides computed in onBoxMove. Apply the same font picker to thumbnail and meme.

topGaps.title: Real product/device mockup library with perspective warp (the Placeit category)
topGaps.approach: We currently only beautify screenshots; the entire Placeit/Smartmockups product mockup category is missing. Bundle a curated set of mockup scene PNGs (apparel, mug, phone/laptop, frame) each with a transparent target region + a baked shading/displacement map. Warp the user's uploaded design into the region via a WebGL homography / displacement shader (glfx.js or a small custom WebGL pass) and multiply-blend the shading layer for realism. No model needed; the cost is asset curation. Start with 6-8 high-value scenes (t-shirt, mug, iPhone, MacBook, poster-frame).

topGaps.title: Wire existing background remover into a 'subject pops in front of text' layer
topGaps.approach: The signature modern YouTube thumbnail is a cut-out person in front of bold text. We already have removeBackground in @/engines/image (proven in studio-sticker). Add a cutout layer drawn AFTER the title so text sits behind the subject, plus a few draggable arrow/circle/emoji overlays. No new model, fully on-device; turns the thumbnail maker from generic into pro.

topGaps.title: Custom module + finder-eye shapes, decorative frames, gradient-true SVG, more payloads
topGaps.approach: Use the qrcode lib's module bit-matrix (we already read pixels in render line 100) to draw rounded/dot modules and styled finder eyes — the main visual differentiator vs QR Tiger. Add a frame+CTA wrapper drawn around the QR, fix downloadSvg to embed a real <linearGradient> so the SVG matches the PNG (currently flattens to g1, line 164), and add vCard/email/SMS/phone/geo payload builders (pure string formatters). Static-only by design (dynamic/tracking needs a server, which the no-server rule forbids).

topGaps.title: Ship a dedicated Background studio (remover + replacer) on the existing engine
topGaps.approach: The hard part (on-device segmentation) already exists as removeBackground in @/engines/image. A standalone Background studio is mostly UI: upload → cutout → pick backdrop (solid / gradient / uploaded image / blurred-original) → optional edge feather → export PNG/JPG. High demand (remove.bg is one of the most-used web tools), very low marginal effort given the engine is in place.

topGaps.title: Drag-to-swap photos, freeform layout mode, text/sticker layer, more layouts + export presets
topGaps.approach: Add HTML5/pointer drag to swap photos between cells and drag-in from a tray (reuse the images map), a freeform mode where cells become draggable/resizable boxes (poster drag model), a text/sticker overlay layer (share the poster layer engine), expand LAYOUT_TEMPLATES to 30+ by photo count, and add 4:5/9:16/custom + JPG/WebP export presets (download() currently PNG-only).

topGaps.title: Multiple resume templates + UI editors for education/skills + content phrase bank + save/load
topGaps.approach: Parameterize the single hardcoded layout into 3-5 template render functions (1-col/2-col/minimal); add the missing add/edit/remove card UIs for education and skills (currently seeded constants with no editor, lines 39-45); add a curated phrase-bank (JSON by job title, no model) for Zety-style bullet suggestions; persist resume data to localStorage and add load/import so a refresh doesn't wipe everything.

topGaps.title: 512x512 messaging export, sticker pack/sheet builder, animated WebP stickers, manual edge brush
topGaps.approach: Add a WhatsApp/Telegram export preset (pad to 512x512, output WebP via canvas.toBlob). Add a pack builder that batches multiple cutouts into a sheet/zip. Add animated stickers (APNG via UPNG.js or animated WebP from canvas frames). Add a manual keep/erase brush to fix bad mattes (share the image studio's layer-mask brush). These make it a real messaging-sticker tool, not just a vinyl-look exporter.
